### `shopping_deposits`

Meta information of the deposit.

`shopping_deposits` is an entity that embodies the specifications for 
incomes and outcomes of deposit at a shopping mall. In other words, 
`shopping_deposits` is not [shopping_deposit_histories](#shopping_deposit_histories), which 
refers to the deposit/outcome details of deposits, but is simply 
metadata that specifies specifications for income/outcome scenarios.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`: Identifier code.
- `source`: The source table occurring the deposit event.
- `direction`
  > Direction of deposit.
  >
  > - `1`: Income
  > - `-1`: outcome
- `created_at`: Creation time of record.
- `deleted_at`: / Deletion time of record.

### `shopping_deposit_histories`

Deposit income/outcome details of customers (citizens).

`shopping_deposit_histories` is an entity that embodies the 
[customer](#shopping_customers)'s income/outcome history.

You can think of it as a kind of accounting ledger table. Therefore, 
note that, `value` must have positive number only, even if it is a 
outcome. The minus value must be expressed by multiplying the 
[shopping_deposits.direction](#shopping_deposits) value of the corresponding.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_deposit_id`: Belonged metadata's [shopping_deposits.id](#shopping_deposits)
- `shopping_citizen_id`: Belonged citizen's [shopping_citizens.id](#shopping_citizens)
- `source_id`: The source record occurred deposit/outcome.
- `value`
  > Income/outcome amount of deposit.
  >
  > It must be a positive number, and you can check
  > [shopping_deposits.direction](#shopping_deposits) for incomes and outcomes.
  > If you want to express the figures for incomes and outcomes as
  > positive/negative numbers, you can also multiply this field value by
  > the attributed [shopping_deposits.direction](#shopping_deposits) value.
- `balance`
  > Balance value.
  >
  > Total balance value after the transaction.
- `created_at`: Creation time of record.
- `cancelled_at`: Cancelled time of record.

### `shopping_deposit_charges`

Deposit deposit.

`shopping_deposit_charges` is an entity that symbolizes the act of a 
[customer](#shopping_customers) applying for a deposit to a shopping 
mall.

However, `shopping_deposit_charges` expresses the customer's intention to 
make a deposit, but it has not yet been confirmed. Only when the customer 
completes the [payment](#shopping_deposit_charge_publishes) 
will the deposit increase be confirmed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_customer_id`: Belonged metadata's [shopping_deposits.id](#shopping_deposits)
- `value`: Charging amount.
- `created_at`: Creation time of record.
- `deleted_at`
  > Deletion time of record.
  >
  > Only when be stopped before publishing.

### `shopping_deposit_charge_publishes`

Payment progress information for deposits.

`shopping_deposit_charge_publishes` is an entity that embodies the process 
of a [customer](#shopping_customers) applying for a deposit and making 
a payment.

Please note that the existence of the `shopping_deposit_charge_publishes` 
record does not mean that payment has been completed. Payment is complete 
only when payment (`paid_at`) is complete. This is what the 
"process of payment" mentioned above means.

However, even after payment has been made, there may be cases where it is 
suddenly cancelled, so you must be careful about this as well.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_deposit_charge_id`: Belonged charge appliance's [shopping_deposit_charges.id](#shopping_deposit_charges)
- `password`
  > Password for encryption.
  >
  > This shopping mall system uses a randomly issued password to encrypt
  > payment history, and is completely unrelated to the user.
- `created_at`
  > Creation time of record.
  >
  > Note that, this property does not mean the payment completion time.
- `paid_at`
  > Completion time of payment.
  >
  > This property is the only way to know if the payment has been
  > completed. If this property is null, the payment has not been
  > completed yet.
- `cancelled_at`: The time when the payment was cancelled or reverted.

### `shopping_mileages`

Meta information of mileage.

`shopping_mileages` is an entity that embodies specifications for mileage 
deposits and outcomes at a shopping mall. In other words, 
`shopping_mileages` is not [shopping_mileage_histories](#shopping_mileage_histories), which means 
mileage deposit and outcome history, but is simply metadata that 
specifies specifications for scenarios in which mileage is deposited and 
withdrawn.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.

- `source`: The source table occurring the mileage event.
- `direction`

  > creating a new record, or percentage value to be applied.
- `created_at`: Creation time of record.
- `deleted_at`: Deletion time of record.

### `shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries`

Inquiry about a sale snapshot.

`shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries` is a subtype entity of 
[bbs_articles](#bbs_articles), and represents inquiries written by 
[customers](#shopping_customers) about a [sale](#shopping_sales) 
registered by the [seller](#shopping_sellers) (however, to trace the
exact [snapshot](#shopping_sale_snapshots), it is referencing not
sale but snapshot).

In addition, since the customer is waiting for the seller's response after 
writing the inquiry, whether the seller has viewed the inquiry written by 
the customer is provided for reference as `read_by_seller_at` property. 
Of course, since the inquiry itself is a subtype of a article, it is also 
possible for sellers to communicate with each other through 
[comments](#shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_comments) before an 
[official response](#shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_responses).

However, comments themselves can be made by every customers, even if they 
are not the person who wrote the article. Of course, it cannot be written 
unless the seller is a party.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: PK + FK.
- `shopping_sale_snapshot_id`: Belonged snapshot's [shopping_sale_snapshots.id](#shopping_sale_snapshots)
- `shopping_customer_id`: Writer customer's [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers)
- `type`
  > Type of the inquiry article.
  >
  > - `question`
  > - `review`
- `created_at`
  > Creation time of record.
  >
  > Duplicated property for fast sorting.
- `read_by_seller_at`: The first time when the seller read the inquiry.

### `shopping_sale_snapshot_questions`

Question about sale snapshot.

`shopping_sale_snapshot_questions` is a subtype entity of 
[shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries](#shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries), and is used when a 
[customer](#shopping_customers) wants to ask something about a 
sale ([snapshot](#shopping_sale_snapshots) at the time) registered by 
the [seller](#shopping_sellers).

And, like most shopping malls, `shopping_sale_snapshot_questions` also 
provides a `secret` attribute, allowing you to create a "secret message" 
that can only be viewed by the seller and the customer who wrote the 
question.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: PK + FK.
- `secret`
  > Whether secret or not.
  >
  > If secret article, only the writer customer and related seller can see
  > the detailed content.

### `shopping_sale_snapshot_reviews`

Reviews for sale snapshots.

`shopping_sale_snapshot_reviews` is a subtype entity of 
[shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries](#shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries), and is used when a 
[customer](#shopping_customers) purchases a sale 
([snapshot](#shopping_sale_snapshots) at the time) registered by the 
[seller](#shopping_sellers) as a product and leaves a review and 
rating for it.

For reference, `shopping_sale_snapshot_reviews` and 
[shopping_order_goods](#shopping_order_goods) have a logarithmic relationship of N: 1, 
but this does not mean that customers can continue to write reviews for 
the same product indefinitely. Wouldn't there be restrictions, such as 
if you write a review once, you can write an additional review a month 
later?

Properties as follows:

- `id`: PK + FK.
- `shopping_order_good_id`: Belonged good's [shopping_order_goods.id](#shopping_order_goods)

### `shopping_sale_snapshot_review_snapshots`

A snapshot of the content of the review for the sale snapshot.

`shopping_sale_snapshot_review_snapshots` is a subtype entity of 
[bbs_article_snapshots](#bbs_article_snapshots) and is designed to add a `score` property 
to the content of [review article](#shopping_sale_snapshot_reviews).

In other words, after writing a review article, customers can edit it 
and change the evaluation `score` at any time.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: PK + FK.
- `score`: Estimation score value.

### `shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_answers`

Answers to inquiries about sale snapshots.

`shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_answers` is an entity that embodies the 
official answer written by the [seller](#shopping_sellers) to the 
[inquiry](#shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries) written by the 
[customer](#shopping_customers).

Of course, in addition to writing an official response like this, it is 
also possible for the seller to communicate with the inquiry written 
customer and multiple customers through 
[comments](#shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_comments) in the 
attribution inquiry.

For reference, it is not possible to write comments on this answer. 
Encourage people to write comments on the inquiry article. This is to 
prevent comments from being scattered in both inquiry and response 
articles.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: PK + FK
- `shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_id`: Belonged inquiry's [shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries.id](#shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries)
- `shopping_seller_customer_id`: Answered seller's [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers)

### `shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_comments`

A comment written on an inquiry article.

`shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_comments` is a subtype entity of 
[bbs_article_comments](#bbs_article_comments), and is used when you want to communicate with 
multiple people about an [inquiry](#shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiries) 
written by a [customer](#shopping_customers).

For reference, only related parties can write comments for 
[sellers](#shopping_sellers), but there is no limit to customers. 
In other words, anyone customer can freely write a comment, even if they are 
not the person who wrote the inquiry.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: PK + FK
- `shopping_customer_id`: Writer's [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers)
- `actor_type`
  > Type of the writer.
  >
  > - customer
  > - seller

`shopping_sale_favorites` is an entity that symbolizes the 
[sale](#shopping_sales) that the [customer](#shopping_customers)

[snapshot](#shopping_sale_snapshots) of the sale at the time when the 
customer favorites it.

- `shopping_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers)

- `shopping_sale_snapshot_id`
  > Target snapshot's [shopping_sale_snapshots.id](#shopping_sale_snapshots)
  >
  > The snapshot of the sale at the time when the customer favorites it.
- `created_at`: Creation time of record.
- `deleted_at`: Deletion time of record.

operations.specification: API operation to create a new 'shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_comments' entity representing a comment written on a product inquiry in the shopping mall system. This entity corresponds to a comment added to an inquiry (question or review) associated with a product's snapshot. The operation should receive all necessary information to initialize a comment, including the reference to the related inquiry, the customer who writes the comment, and content details. As per the Prisma schema, each comment record is a subtype of 'bbs_article_comments', uniquely identified by its UUID, and may include hierarchical relationships for replies, actor_type (customer/seller), and the relevant inquiry ID. Business logic includes validating that only authorized actors (such as the related customer or seller) can comment, applying moderation rules, and ensuring evidence preservation through snapshot linkage. Security, audit logging, and relationship integrity to 'shopping_customers' and 'bbs_article_comments' are required.
operations.description: This POST operation enables a customer or seller to add a comment to an inquiry (either question or review) made on a product listed via a sale snapshot. The new comment will be created as a new 'shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_comments' entity and will internally link to the corresponding 'bbs_article_comments' base record for content and versioning purposes. User permissions are checked to ensure that only appropriate actors (e.g., inquiry author, seller, or other customers) can comment. Hierarchical replies are supported if a parent comment ID is provided. The request must specify the related inquiry, the actor role (customer or seller), and the comment content. The operation audits account for moderation or deletion cases, recording evidence for disputes and ensuring compliance with e-commerce and privacy policies. Validation includes checking that the referenced inquiry exists and that the user acting is authorized. Related endpoints include inquiry fetching, comment listing, and comment deletion or update endpoints.

Allows modification of the content and potentially hierarchical reply relationships (parent-child). Uses the UUID-based identifier as per the Prisma schema to reference the specific comment to be updated. Enforces business rules to prevent unauthorized edits, such as limiting updates to the original author or administrators and preserving change history by updating the underlying snapshot in 'bbs_article_comment_snapshots'. Operation includes content validation, permission checks, and audit logging for evidence preservation.
operations.description: This PUT operation updates the content or structure of an existing product inquiry comment (represented by 'shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_comments'), identified by the unique UUID in the path. It ensures that only authorized users (e.g., the original author or system administrator where permitted) can make changes and that edits are appropriately versioned to maintain audit trails, complying with e-commerce evidence-preservation standards. Changes are reflected in the base 'bbs_article_comments' and an updated comment snapshot is created to record version history. Input includes editable fields such as new content, parent comment reference for hierarchical structures, or meta fields if allowed. Errors are returned if the comment does not exist, the actor lacks permission, or the update violates business rules (e.g., editing after deletion). Related endpoints: create, fetch, and delete comment operations for the same entity.

According to the 'shopping_orders' schema, each record encompasses properties such as the related customer, associated address, representative name, monetary distributions across payment methods (cash, deposit, mileage), and timestamps for creation or potential deletion. This endpoint is essential for clients or administrative processes to retrieve the full context of an order—including its payment and fulfillment status, billing, and delivery address.

Security: Access to this endpoint may be limited to authenticated users, sellers, or administrators with the necessary role permissions. The detailed order object returned follows permission boundaries, avoiding leakage of sensitive data if requested by unauthorized actors.

Errors: If the specified order ID does not exist, the API should return a 404 Not Found error. Permission errors must return 403 Forbidden. Referenced columns, such as shopping_customer_id, shopping_address_id, and monetary distributions, should be accurately populated according to schema comments.

This operation may be used in conjunction with endpoints listing orders, placing new orders, or managing customer activities. It complements the CRUD suite by providing direct retrieval of individual order resources.

operations.description:
This endpoint enables clients to submit new order applications to the system. According to the 'shopping_orders' schema, the payload must include core properties such as the related customer, address for delivery (optional), order representative name, and payment distributions (cash, deposit, mileage). Upon submission, the backend must validate required data, transform relevant shopping cart commodities into order goods, and ensure business logic adherence like checking item availability and appropriate payment allocation.

Security: Only authenticated customers are authorized to place orders. The operation may trigger additional system behaviors, such as stock validation, discount application, order value reconciliations, and analytics logging.

Validation rules include verifying non-negative payment values, ensuring customer, and (optionally) address relationships exist, and checking for constraints such as payments being logically distributed. Duplicate or erroneous submissions will be flagged with descriptive errors (400 or 409 status codes). Upon success, the created order details are returned for immediate reference.

Related APIs to pre-execute may include: fetching the customer cart, validating inventory, and calculating final prices prior to placement.

operations.description:
This operation enables clients to update the details of a specific shopping order by its unique order ID. Modifiable fields could include delivery address, order representative name, and distributions among payment methods, provided the order is still in a modifiable state (i.e., before payment confirmation). Backend logic must verify the order's state, permitting updates only when allowed per business rules referenced in the 'shopping_orders' schema and requirement analysis. Attempts to update non-modifiable or confirmed orders must yield an error.

Security: Only the original customer, or authorized administrators, should be able to update orders. Changes are logged for audit trails, in compliance with evidence preservation requirements.

This operation is closely related to the order retrieval and creation endpoints, forming part of the complete order management lifecycle in the shopping system.

If the order ID does not exist, return 404; on validation failure, return 400; permission errors yield 403.

The operation ensures that references to this order (such as goods, payments, or delivery records) remain consistent for historical review, analytics, or dispute resolution.

Security: Only administrators or the original customer (within business-defined boundaries) can request deletion. Attempts to delete non-existent orders return 404; permission errors return 403. The endpoint should return a status indicating the deletion result, along with the updated record if needed.

This operation complements the get, create, and update endpoints and must be coordinated with order status to prevent deletion of already finalized, paid, or delivered orders.

This operation is only allowed if the item has not already been converted into an order. Business logic may trigger recalculation of cart totals and save updated session state. Error responses include not found, forbidden, and conflict errors when cart state is invalid. This operation fetches a single coupon funnel criteria based on its ID for administrative purposes or for rendering application constraints on coupon issuance/use. It ensures that tailored criteria such as access path, referrer, or variable are properly exposed to the frontend for validation or configuration. Access to this endpoint should be restricted to users with coupon management permissions. Error handling should communicate non-existence or insufficient permission cases clearly.
operations.description:
This endpoint retrieves a single coupon funnel criteria by its unique identifier. Coupon funnel criterias define access limitations for coupon usage/issuance, such as requiring users to access the system via a specified referral path or URL parameter. The Prisma schema comment emphasizes these criterias can control funnel restrictions in three ways: path, referrer, or variable (custom key/value pairs) for targeted coupon campaigns. Funnel criterias are critical for controlling coupon acquisition/usage in marketing and fraud prevention.

Internally, this endpoint queries the shopping_coupon_funnel_criterias table using the provided ID, returning detailed information about the funnel's kind, key (when applicable), and value. Sensitive information may require masking depending on operator role. Error responses are provided for nonexistent IDs or unauthorized access.

This endpoint is typically accessed by coupon system administrators when managing targeted campaigns or analyzing coupon effectiveness. It complements endpoints for listing, creating, updating, or deleting criteria, allowing for comprehensive coupon funnel management workflows.

This endpoint allows for the creation of a new coupon funnel criteria, as defined in the Prisma schema for shopping_coupon_funnel_criterias. Funnel criterias are used to restrict coupon availability or usage to users coming through certain paths (URLs), referrers, or custom variables (key-value pairs). This is essential for both marketing efforts (targeting users via landing pages) and fraud prevention. The request body must specify the kind (path, referrer, variable), the value, and, if kind is variable, the key as well. All entries are subject to format validation according to marketing and compliance policies.

Upon success, the endpoint inserts a new record into shopping_coupon_funnel_criterias with the provided criteria and sequence order if required. Administrators must ensure that these settings do not conflict with existing coupon issuance workflows and that appropriate error handling is in place for invalid or conflicting data. Once created, these funnel criterias become available for assignment to specific coupons or campaigns.

Operators can update any field, such as kind (path, referrer, variable), value, and, for variables, the key. The endpoint supports partial or full updates, enforcing business logic (e.g., maintaining existing constraints and campaign coherence).

Security context and auditing are important—each update action should log the operator and changes made. After updating, the modified record is returned. If the specified ID does not exist or the operator lacks permissions, an error is returned. To prevent disruptions in live campaigns, rigorous validation and/or operator warnings may apply when modifying active funnel criterias.

Query parameters and advanced search in the request body allow filtering by customer, coupon, issue/expiration date, usage status, etc.

Access security ensures only appropriate users or administrators can fetch relevant tickets; privacy controls apply for customer self-service.

Returns the complete details of the ticket or an error. Appropriate masking of sensitive information (if any) is performed depending on user role. shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
ID of the sale snapshot ({@link shopping_sale_snapshots.id}) this unit belongs to.

Required to associate the unit with a particular version of a product's configuration. Enforces referential integrity and supports audit and legal traceability.

name.description:

Must be unique within the belonging snapshot. As per schema comment, conveys both product display and internal mapping. This title is typically visible in product configuration screens and analytics.

primary.description:
Label indicating if this unit is the most important component among the bundle (primary true/false).

May inform UI display strategies or logic determining purchase flow requirements.

required.description:
Indicates whether it is mandatory for a customer to select this unit as part of the purchase configuration.

Directly supports business rules on product bundling: items like 'Main Body' are required, while 'Accessory' may be optional.

sequence.description:
The ordering number of this unit relative to other units in the same sale snapshot.

Used for explicit product configuration sequence on UI and in the backend, relevant to logical/evidence order in dispute situations.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.ICreate.description: Request body type for creating a sale snapshot unit in the system (shopping_sale_snapshot_units). Represents a component in a product's offered configuration. All properties are required to ensure full provenance, logical ordering, and audit trail alignment as described in the DB schema.

name.description:
Representative name of the unit. Allows edit for display/user context or correction.

Should preserve context, preserve uniqueness if updated.

primary.description:
Whether the unit is considered primary after the update.

Supports dynamic re-labelling of product components post-registration.

required.description:
Flag to adjust whether this unit must be included in a purchase.

May impact validation flows on the customer-facing and admin side.

sequence.description: Update to the sequence/order within the sale snapshot for display/configuration logic.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.IUpdate.description: Request body type for updating an existing sale snapshot unit. Every property is optional to support PATCH-style partial update semantics. Only permitted fields may be changed, enforcing schema and evidence preservation requirements.

success.description: Indicates whether the delete operation was successful.

message.description: Optional human-readable detail about the result of the delete operation, e.g., reason for failure.

IDeleteResponse.description: Standardized API response type indicating the result of a delete operation. Used for both hard and soft (logical) delete endpoints. Provides success boolean and optional message for diagnostics or UI feedback.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_id.description:

type.description:
Filter: Option type. Valid values include: 'select', 'string', 'boolean', 'number'.

May be used to refine results by structural/semantic meaning in product configuration logic.

name.description:
Search/filter: Option name or partial match.

Supports UI searching, admin analytics, or troubleshooting workflows.

page.description: Result page for pagination (1-based index). Default: 1.

limit.description: Number of records per page for pagination. Default: 20 or system preset.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOption.IRequest.description:

Strict parameter validation required, and all searches are audit-logged as per e-commerce system requirements.

data.description: List of sale snapshot unit option summary/domain objects on the returned page.

IPageISaleSnapshotUnitOption.description:
Container type holding a page of ISaleSnapshotUnitOption records, as per system-wide standard paging structure (see IPage<T>). Results are guaranteed to have both high-level pagination details and the current page's data array.

Pagination object per shared IPage spec; data is the slice of requested entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the sale snapshot unit option. DB: {@link shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_options.id}

Essential for linking to candidates and evidentiary audit history.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_id.description:
Reference to parent unit. DB: {@link shopping_sale_snapshot_units.id}

Facilitates hierarchical search, display, and integrity enforcement.

name.description:
Display name/title for the option (e.g., 'Color', 'Size').

Business rules may require name uniqueness per unit; supports user UX, analytics, and evidence trails.

type.description:
Type of the option control. Valid values are: 'select' (pick a value), 'string' (free text), 'boolean' (checkbox), 'number' (numeric input).

Directly drives UI rendering and analytics. Schema drives core business logic and evidence policies.

variable.description:
Indicates whether this option is variable (affects final product stock/inventory). See schema for critical conditional logic.

Variable 'select'-type options split stocks; others are metadata.

sequence.description: Order index for displaying options in configuration UI. Also used for evidence order during disputes.

candidates.description: The array of selectable candidate values for this option (only required for 'select'-type options). Preserved for audit, UI, and validation.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOption.description: Response and reference type for an individual sale snapshot unit option in product configuration. Represents one selectable or informational characteristic of a product unit. Candidates field holds possible values for 'select'-type options.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_id.description:
Parent unit in which to create the option. Refers to DB: {@link shopping_sale_snapshot_units.id}

Required for linking and validates existence.

name.description:
Display name for the new option (e.g., 'Color').

Should be unique within the unit to avoid ambiguity, as per schema and business rule specifications.

type.description:
Option type, one of 'select', 'string', 'boolean', 'number'.

Critical attribute for system and UI logic enforcement.

variable.description:
If true, this option will determine inventory/stock splits, permitted only for 'select'-type. Otherwise, it is immaterial for system splitting logic.

Non-variable options are meta only; see schema policy.

sequence.description: Ordering number for UI display and evidence/analytics sequence.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOption.ICreate.description: Create type for a new sale snapshot unit option in the product system. All fields required to ensure entity integrity, unique identification, and correct propagation into evidence/audit chains and the customer UI.

name.description: Update to the option name, affecting UI and analytics but must respect uniqueness per unit.

type.description: Change of option type ('select', 'string', 'boolean', 'number'). Highly regulated; may force backend validation or migration of candidate values.

variable.description: May change if business rules and reference integrity allow. Only meaningful for 'select' type in current spec.

sequence.description: Update to display/order index for option listings.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOption.IUpdate.description: Update schema for sale snapshot unit options. Allows for partial updates (PATCH semantics). Only permitted fields are available, conforming to evidence-preserving schema. Strict backend validation applies.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_option_id.description:
Filter: Parent option to search candidate values for ({@link shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_options.id}).

Enables search, consistency, and efficient UI.

name.description: Filter: Candidate value name, supports partial match or exact search.

limit.description: Maximum results per page.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOptionCandidate.IReques.description: Request body for searching and paginating candidate values for a sale snapshot unit option—see DB comments for stock-combinatorial logic. Permits searching on parent option ID, candidate name, and utilizes common pagination concepts. All fields validated for system security and auditing.

data.description: Paginated array of option candidate objects.

IPageISaleSnapshotUnitOptionCandidate.description: Paginated result set for sale snapshot unit option candidates. Contains page metadata as per system IPage interface and current slice of candidate objects. Used in all candidate-listing endpoints for stock/option configuration.

id.description:
Unique identifier (UUID) for the candidate value record ({@link shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_option_candidates.id}).

Integral for option splitting and evidence preservation.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_option_id.description:
Parent option ID. Relates to {@link shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_options.id}.

Hierarchical integrity, required for search and UI rendering.

name.description:
Display value of the candidate (e.g., 8GB, Red, Large, RTX 4080).

Must be unique within the option for correct product configuration logic and consistent user experience.

sequence.description: Sequence/order index. Used for UI ordering and logical evidence presentation.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOptionCandidate.description: Response and reference type for a selectable candidate value to a unit's option (for 'select'-type options only). Represents one possible value in a configurable set for a customer and is required for evidence in option/stock splitting.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_option_id.description:
Parent option of the candidate ({@link shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_options.id}).

Required for integrity. Must reference existing option and comply with option type 'select'.

name.description:
Candidate value to add (display name in UI and stock logic).

Must be unique for parent option per schema policy and business rule.

sequence.description: Order of display; relevant for UI and dispute resolution evidence.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOptionCandidate.ICreate.description: Creation schema for an option candidate value for a sale snapshot unit option. All required fields necessary to link, order, and evidence the candidate in the system for robust option/stock/taxonomy configuration.

limit.description: Page size (maximum entities per page).

records.description: Total number of records matching the search/filter parameters.

pages.description: Total number of result pages given page size and record count; ceil(records/limit).

page.description: The page number for pagination. Optional; if omitted, defaults to the first page.

limit.description: Number of records per page.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stock_id.description: Filter: Retrieve only inventory supplementation records belonging to this particular unit stock (shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stock_id). Reference: Prisma schema column 'shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stock_id'.

created_at_from.description: Filter: ISO8601 start date for supplement creation. Use to search supplements created after this datetime.

created_at_to.description: Filter: ISO8601 end date for supplement creation. Use to search supplements created before this datetime.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnitStockSupplement.description: Request payload for searching and paginating inventory supplementation records (shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stock_supplements). Includes filters for pagination, range searching, and association by parent stock. All fields reflect the audit and evidence requirements rooted in the business and Prisma data model.

data.description: List of supplementation records (unit stock inventory additions) included in this page.

IPageIShoppingSaleSnapshotUnitStockSuppl.description: A paginated result set for inventory supplementation (shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stock_supplements). This structure is used for listing inventory supplements with contextual pagination meta information. Match with the standard IPage<T> pagination model.

id.description: Primary key. Uniquely identifies the supplementation record. References Prisma column 'id'.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stock_id.description: Foreign key: The unit stock associated with this supplementation (references shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stocks.id).

quantity.description: The quantity of inventory supplemented. This is a positive integer indicating units added. Originates from the 'quantity' column in Prisma.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the supplementation was recorded. References Prisma column 'created_at'.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnitStockSupplement.description: Represents the supplementation event of inventory quantity for a specific unit stock (shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stocks). Each record denotes when and how much the inventory was increased as per the sales/inventory management business rules. This structure preserves historical evidence and full traceability as described in evidence management and legal compliance system requirements.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stock_id.description: Reference to the target unit stock being supplemented. (Prisma: shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stocks.id).

quantity.description: The non-negative integer for quantity being added. Must be a positive value per business/prisma rules.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnitStockSupplement.description: The request body for creating a new supplementation record for inventory (shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_stock_supplements). Incoming data must specify the target unit stock and supplementation quantity.

quantity.description: Updated inventory supplementation quantity. Should always be positive and typically only allowed if the record is not locked for audit or already used in downstream operations.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnitStockSupplement.description: Request body for updating an existing supplementation record for inventory quantity. Only specific fields (typically quantity) may be updated as per business and compliance logic.

shopping_channel_category_id.description: Search filter by channel category being linked. (Prisma: shopping_channel_category_id)

IPageIShoppingSaleSnapshotCategory.description: Paginated result set structure for sale snapshot category mappings. Allows UIs and analytics to consume lists of sale-to-category assignments in a paginated/filtered manner.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description: Foreign key: Sale snapshot being categorized. References Prisma: 'shopping_sale_snapshot_id'.

shopping_channel_category_id.description: Foreign key: Channel category to which the sale snapshot is assigned. References Prisma: 'shopping_channel_category_id'.

sequence.description: Sequence/order number for display or business logic. Originates in the Prisma column 'sequence'.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotCategory.description: Sale snapshot category assignment record (shopping_sale_snapshot_categories). Associates a product sale snapshot to a specific channel category with explicit ordering, supporting business analytics, display, and dynamic taxonomy control as required for omnichannel e-commerce operations.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description: The snapshot of sale being categorized (shopping_sale_snapshot_id).

sequence.description: Order/sequence number for deterministic display or processing.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotCategory.ICreate.description: Request body schema for creating a new link between a sale snapshot and a channel category. Used to assign, rearrange, or display a sale in multiple categories as per retail/ERP requirements.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotCategory.IUpdate.description: Request body schema for updating a sale snapshot category assignment (e.g., changing order or sequence). Normally, only certain fields are updatable per system rules.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotContent.description: Detailed content record for a sale snapshot (Prisma: shopping_sale_snapshot_contents table). Includes all textual and auxiliary data for presentation, legal compliance, and audit purposes.

Follows the IPage<T> pattern designed for scalable APIs where product sales are listed with page information for efficient UI navigation. The 'data' array consists of IShoppingSale objects representing individual product sales, while 'pagination' supplies current page, record counts, and page boundaries.

See the original IPage<T> comment for further information on usage and pagination fields.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for the product sale record.

shopping_section_id.description:
ID of the section (spatial area/corner) this sale belongs to.

shopping_seller_customer_id.description:

Creation time of the sale record.

Opening time of the sale. If null, not open yet.

opened_at.description:
Opening time of the sale. If null, not open yet.

closed_at.description:
Closing time of the sale. Null if the sale is perpetual.

oneOf.description:
Time when seller paused the sale for any reason.

paused_at.description:
Time when seller paused the sale for any reason.

suspended_at.description:
Timestamp when the sale was suspended by the seller or the system.

IShoppingSale.description:
Represents a single product sale entry registered by a seller.

The core sale record captures the linkage between sellers and market spatial sections, along with status tracking for open, closed, paused, and suspended sales. Detailed product content, pricing, and configuration are handled through related snapshot and subordinate entities.

All fields below are mapped and documented with attention to their corresponding Prisma schema columns for evidence preservation and traceability in legal or business contexts.

shopping_section_id.description:
ID of the section (market area) this sale is registered in.

This is a required field during sale creation.

References shopping_sections.id from the Prisma schema.

shopping_seller_customer_id.description:
ID of the seller's customer record for this sale listing.

References shopping_customers.id from the Prisma schema. Required to assign the ownership of the sale record to a specific seller.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Opening time for this sale. If omitted or null, the sale is not currently open and requires later activation by the seller or general process.

References shopping_sales.opened_at in Prisma.

opened_at.description:
(Optional) Opening time for this sale. If omitted or null, the sale is not currently open and requires later activation by the seller or general process.

References shopping_sales.opened_at in Prisma.

IShoppingSale.ICreate.description:
Schema for registering a new product sale by a seller (creation POST operation).

Takes input for spatial section and seller, as well as (optionally) the opening time. The ID and creation timestamp are not client-supplied but are assigned automatically by the backend. Mapped from the shopping_sales model in Prisma.

Required for product sale registration workflows, ensuring valid section/seller linkage upon creation.

shopping_section_id.description:
(Optional) Updated section ID for the product sale listing.

If the product moves to a new spatial section in the mall, this value is supplied here.

References shopping_sections.id in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Update the opening time. Null means unset or not open yet.

References shopping_sales.opened_at in the Prisma schema.

opened_at.description:
(Optional) Update the opening time. Null means unset or not open yet.

References shopping_sales.opened_at in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Update the closing time for the sale, or set null for indefinite.

References shopping_sales.closed_at in Prisma.

closed_at.description:
(Optional) Update the closing time for the sale, or set null for indefinite.

References shopping_sales.closed_at in Prisma.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Update the paused time for this sale.

References shopping_sales.paused_at in the Prisma schema.

paused_at.description:
(Optional) Update the paused time for this sale.

References shopping_sales.paused_at in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Update/inject suspended timestamp for the sale.

Used for marking the sale suspended (manually or automatically per business logic).

References shopping_sales.suspended_at from the Prisma schema.

suspended_at.description:
(Optional) Update/inject suspended timestamp for the sale.

Used for marking the sale suspended (manually or automatically per business logic).

References shopping_sales.suspended_at from the Prisma schema.

IShoppingSale.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating a product sale entry.

All fields are optional—client supplies only those to be updated. This schema covers status transitions of sale records including opening, closing, pausing, and suspending sales. Leveraged by seller/admin update operations mapped to shopping_sales table in Prisma.

Required for sale lifecycle management workflows and audit compliance.

shopping_sale_id.description:
(Optional) Filter by sale ID to retrieve snapshots of a specific sale.

Reference: shopping_sale_snapshots.shopping_sale_id in the Prisma schema.

created_from.description:
(Optional) Filter for snapshots created after this timestamp.

Reference: created_at in shopping_sale_snapshots.

created_to.description:
(Optional) Filter for snapshots created before this timestamp.

Reference: created_at in shopping_sale_snapshots.

limit.description: Maximum number of snapshot records per page (pagination).

IShoppingSaleSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Request structure for searching or listing product sale snapshots.

Includes filters for sale ID and creation timestamp range. Pagination controls are supplied for efficient UI navigation and to handle high-volume snapshot data.

All properties map to fields or query scenarios supported by shopping_sale_snapshots in Prisma, implementing compliance for evidence preservation and audit trails.

IPageShoppingSaleSnapshot.description:
A paginated result list of product sale snapshot records.

Conforms to the IPage<T> interface, with 'data' array containing IShoppingSaleSnapshot entities and 'pagination' field representing current page, counts, and record bounds.

Frequently used in APIs supporting browsing, analysis, or evidence gathering for product configuration histories.

id.description:
Primary key of this sale snapshot record.

References shopping_sale_snapshots.id from Prisma.

shopping_sale_id.description:
ID of parent sale to which this snapshot belongs.

References shopping_sales.id.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when this snapshot was created.

References shopping_sale_snapshots.created_at.

IShoppingSaleSnapshot.description:
A historical or current configuration snapshot of a product sale.

Contains immutable records for a product's key configuration state at a single moment in time—supporting versioned product details, pricing, and compliance evidence for legal or business reasons. Further details (units, content, etc.) reside in subordinate or related entities as per the Prisma schema.

Each field maps to a corresponding Prisma schema property for reliable cross-reference and audit trail integrity.

shopping_sale_id.description:
Sale ID for which a new snapshot will be produced.

Requirement: must reference a valid existing sale (shopping_sales.id).

Required upon creation.

IShoppingSaleSnapshot.ICreate.description:
Schema for creating a new product sale snapshot record.

Enables sellers/admins to register a new historical version of a sale, fulfilling requirements for evidence, versioning, and auditability in the shopping system. The only field required from client is the sale reference; all other details are managed by related subordinate creation endpoints or automated by the backend.

Directly references shopping_sale_snapshots in Prisma.

IShoppingSaleSnapshot.IUpdate.description:
No fields are directly updatable for product sale snapshot records.

Sale snapshot entries are designed to be immutable for evidence and audit compliance. Any changes must be realized by inserting new snapshots, not updating existing ones. Use this schema for API interface consistency only.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
(Optional) Filter by snapshot ID to narrow results to units of a single product sale snapshot.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.shopping_sale_snapshot_id.

name.description:
(Optional) Filter by the name of the product unit (supports partial matching).

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.name.

primary.description:
(Optional) Filter for required (primary) units.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.primary.

required.description:
(Optional) Filter for whether the unit is required to be chosen in a product configuration.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.required.

limit.description: Page size for pagination.

page.description: Page number for paginated result sets.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.IRequest.description:
Structure for listing or searching product unit records inside sale snapshots.

Fields allow filtering by snapshot, name, or flags for primary/required units. Pagination is enabled and aligned with best practices for scalable search and UI display. Type maps to shopping_sale_snapshot_units and related search fields in Prisma.

IPageShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.description:
Paginated wrapper of product unit records for a snapshot.

Implements the IPage<T> pagination and search interface with an array of IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit objects and pagination metadata. Used for configuration wizards, bulk inventory management, and UI presentation of product bundles/options.

id.description:
Primary key for the product unit in the sale snapshot.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.id in Prisma.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
ID of the sale snapshot this unit belongs to.

References shopping_sale_snapshots.id.

name.description:
Display name of the product unit (e.g., Main Body, Keyboard).

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.name in Prisma.

primary.description:
Indicates if this unit is primary for the configuration (label only).

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.primary flag.

required.description:
Indicates if the unit must be selected for any purchase under this sale snapshot.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.required flag.

sequence.description:
Ordering of this unit within the sale snapshot for presentation or processing purposes.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.sequence.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.description:
Describes a single product unit as registered within a specific sale snapshot.

Stores all relevant attributes for bundled goods, product components, or options—label, display, and configuration flags. Each record is associated to a parent snapshot for versioning and audit traceability. All fields trace directly back to columns in the shopping_sale_snapshot_units table for reliable system mapping and legal compliance.

limit.description: Items per page, default 100.

pages.description: Total number of available pages, ceiling division of total records by limit.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata.

Included in all paginated responses. Shows current page, record limits, and page total information. Follows IPage.IPagination as described in documentation.

shopping_mileage_id.description:
The unique identifier of the mileage specification ('shopping_mileages') to which this transaction pertains.

Referenced from the 'shopping_mileage_histories' schema: relates this transaction to a particular scenario, such as earning or using points, based on events like purchases, campaigns, or admin grants.

shopping_citizen_id.description:
The unique identifier of the citizen (user) associated with this mileage record.

Per 'shopping_mileage_histories' in the schema, this field indicates the recipient (income) or spender (outcome) of the mileage transaction.

source_id.description:
A reference to the source record that generated this mileage transaction (e.g., payment, campaign, admin action).

According to the schema, this enables per-event tracing and supports evidence and dispute tracking.

value.description:
The actual mileage amount added or used, according to the transaction direction specified in the mileage metadata. Must always be a positive number, even for outcomes.

From the DB schema: positive only, direction handled by referenced 'shopping_mileages.direction'.

balance.description:
The new balance for the user after transaction. Used to keep a running total after the action, supports real-time user balance monitoring and accounting compliance.

Schema: the resulting balance following this mileage event.

IMileageHistory.ICreate.description:
Represents information required to create a new mileage history transaction. Each record logs mileage accrual or outcome (usage), required for point-based accounting, user reward programs, and evidence preservation. Fields mirror those of the schema: 'shopping_mileage_histories'.

This structure is crucial for preserving a clear record of every point alteration in the system, including the source event, the participant, and the magnitude of the change. The immutable history supports legal evidence in case of disputes as per the requirements specification.

value.description:
If adjusting mileage value is permitted by policy, this specifies the corrected point value for this transaction. Still must always be positive, with sign determined by 'direction' in the referenced mileage meta.

Directly modifies the value recorded for the transaction per audit and correctional needs.

balance.description:
If adjusting user mileage balance is required (for reconciliation, admin intervention, or audit correction), provides the new balance after the transaction.

Helps maintain a correct running user total as per accounting/auditing.

cancelled_at.description:

Links the journey step to the specific delivery process it belongs to. A delivery may have multiple associated journey steps representing phases such as preparation, shipping, and completion.

Phase type or stage in the delivery process. Examples include 'preparing', 'manufacturing', 'shipping', 'delivering'.

Defines the logical state in the delivery workflow; values are typically drawn from a controlled list mandated by system requirements. Enables precise traceability of status throughout the logistics chain.

oneOf.description:

Useful for display in logistics dashboards or to clarify custom workflow steps.

description.description:
Optional further explanation or notes about the journey step.

May contain free-text explanations, special instructions, or operator remarks for each phase of the delivery process.

sequence.description:
Sequence or order of this journey step within a delivery.

Numeric value enables the system to sort and present multiple journey records in logical chronological or business-defined order.

created_at.description:

Serves as the main audit field for tracking journey initialization or workflow progression. Reflects the record's creation in the system, not necessarily the real-world event.

oneOf.description:

Enables precise tracking of logistics or production flows—important for SLAs and BI analysis.

started_at.description:
Optional timestamp when this journey step actually started.

Enables precise tracking of logistics or production flows—important for SLAs and BI analysis.

completed_at.description:

Combined with 'started_at', supports lead-time and delay analytics, as well as customer-facing delivery status screens.

IShoppingDeliveryJourney.description:
Represents a single step (or phase) in the delivery process for a shopping mall order shipment, according to the 'shopping_delivery_journeys' Prisma schema. Each delivery consists of one or more journey records sequenced to mirror the package's path through the fulfillment pipeline (e.g., preparation, shipping, delivery completion).

Each journey captures audit fields, phase/type, and metadata. This supports analytics, SLA compliance, logistics optimization, and dispute resolution. Key journey types and their transitions are critical for timeline accuracy, customer notifications, and legal evidence.

shopping_delivery_id.description:
Required. Reference to the delivery record to which this journey belongs. Must match an existing 'shopping_deliveries' record.

Ensures correct linkage between a journey step and its delivery context.

type.description:
Required. Type or phase of journey step (e.g., 'preparing', 'manufacturing', 'shipping', 'delivering'). See requirements for permitted values.

Supported values and business logic may vary by system customization and should be enforced at the application or API layer.

oneOf.description:
Optional. Short title for this delivery journey phase.

Useful for labeling workflow steps for display or BO dashboards.

title.description:
Optional. Short title for this delivery journey phase.

Useful for labeling workflow steps for display or BO dashboards.

oneOf.description:
Optional. Human-readable explanation or notes for the journey entry.

Allows operators to specify additional details at each phase.

description.description:
Optional. Human-readable explanation or notes for the journey entry.

Allows operators to specify additional details at each phase.

sequence.description:
Required. Position of this journey step within the delivery's journey sequence.

Ensures correct business ordering of delivery phases. Sequencing must avoid duplicates per delivery.

oneOf.description:
Optional. If journey starts immediately upon creation, this field can be pre-filled (for corner-cases or backfilling prior records).

Represents the actual start time of the phase, not just when the model was created.

started_at.description:
Optional. If journey starts immediately upon creation, this field can be pre-filled (for corner-cases or backfilling prior records).

Represents the actual start time of the phase, not just when the model was created.

oneOf.description:
Optional. If the journey step is already completed at creation (data migration, rapid progression), include the actual completion timestamp here.

Application logic determines if this state can be applied at creation or must be left null.

completed_at.description:
Optional. If the journey step is already completed at creation (data migration, rapid progression), include the actual completion timestamp here.

Application logic determines if this state can be applied at creation or must be left null.

IShoppingDeliveryJourney.ICreate.description:
Input type for registering a new delivery journey record in the mall system, following the 'shopping_delivery_journeys' Prisma model. Used for POST operations where a logistics phase, such as 'shipping' or 'preparation', is registered for traceability.

Captures both minimal required fields (journey type/phase, sequence, delivery reference), and optional audit/time fields if relevant (e.g. for migration, pre-filled status, or batch backfill). Does not require an explicit ID—the system will generate it.

type.description:
Optionally update the journey phase/type, if business rules permit.

Used to correct misclassification or reflect workflow changes (e.g., business process retriage).

completed_at.description: Optional. Update or set the phase's actual completion time.

Should only be set by backend, admin, or system API, not from normal user flows.

deleted_at.description:
Optional. Set if the record is being (logically) deleted at this moment (for soft delete tracking).

Should only be set by backend, admin, or system API, not from normal user flows.

Update type for an existing delivery journey step in the mall system, mapping to 'shopping_delivery_journeys' update operations. Accepts all fields that may be changed (phase, title, audit fields) except for immutable references (ID, parent delivery).

Supports patch/update for sequence correction, workflow edits, or reclassification. Business logic determines which transitions are permitted in practice (cannot undelete, may not move to certain phases without preconditions, etc.).

IShoppingCoupon.description:
A discount coupon metadata record, conforming to 'shopping_coupons' Prisma schema. Contains all configuration and audit fields required to implement advanced campaign logic, eligibility, issuance/usage restrictions, and expiration control.

Critical for marketing campaign analysis, customer loyalty workflows, and compliance reporting.

shopping_customer_id.description:
Required. Reference to the creator's customer record (seller or admin).

Links this coupon to its creating entity for admin/audit traceability and campaign analytics.

actor_type.description: Required. 'administrator' or 'seller'. Explicitly denotes creator's business context and sets constraints on permitted configurations.

name.description: Required. Coupon display name for UI and admin oversight.

access.description: Required. 'public' or 'private'—access mode for discoverability and claim workflow.

exclusive.description: Required. Whether this is an exclusive coupon (cannot be stacked with others in a single order).

value.description: Required. For 'amount', value in currency; for 'percent', value 0~100.

oneOf.description: Optional. Minimum order total for coupon validity.

threshold.description: Optional. Minimum order total for coupon validity.

oneOf.description: Optional. Maximum discount value for a single use. If set, caps discounts for high-value orders.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum discount value for a single use. If set, caps discounts for high-value orders.

multiplicative.description: Required. If true (and unit='amount'), the discount can be multiplied by quantity ordered.

oneOf.description: Optional. Total allowed tickets for this coupon (null means unlimited).

volume.description: Optional. Total allowed tickets for this coupon (null means unlimited).

oneOf.description:
Optional. Tickets per eligible customer/citizen (null means unlimited per customer).

System should check this on ticket claim.

volume_per_citizen.description:
Optional. Tickets per eligible customer/citizen (null means unlimited per customer).

System should check this on ticket claim.

oneOf.description: Optional. Number of days after claim until ticket expires (null means use global/absolute expiry only).

expired_in.description: Optional. Number of days after claim until ticket expires (null means use global/absolute expiry only).

oneOf.description: Optional. Absolute expiration date for all tickets issued under this coupon.

expired_at.description: Optional. Absolute expiration date for all tickets issued under this coupon.

oneOf.description: Optional. Time the coupon becomes available (null means immediately active).

opened_at.description: Optional. Time the coupon becomes available (null means immediately active).

oneOf.description: Optional. Last possible time for ticket issuance/claiming (null means only limited by general expiry or stock).

closed_at.description: Optional. Last possible time for ticket issuance/claiming (null means only limited by general expiry or stock).

volume.description: Optional. Update total ticket volume cap; only possible if no tickets are issued yet.

opened_at.description: Optional. Schedule or reschedule start date of coupon validity.

ISaleSnapshotContentThumbnail.IUpdate.description:

This type is used for updating properties such as sequence (display order) or associated file in the shopping mall's sale snapshot content thumbnail system. ISaleSnapshotTag.description:
Sale snapshot tag data object.

Represents a tag keyword/text string attached to a sale snapshot, used for search, SEO, or categorization of products. Directly reflects a row in the `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags` Prisma table.

Includes tag metadata (value, sequence) and references to snapshot ID. Used throughout frontend batch operations, search, and administrative UIs for tag management.

References: Prisma `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags`.

Tagging system supports uniqueness and ordering per snapshot for precise search optimization.

id.description:
Primary key. Unique identifier for this tag record.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.id`.

FK to the snapshot this tag annotates.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.shopping_sale_snapshot_id`. References the product's versioned snapshot.

value.description:
Actual tag keyword/text. Used for product keyword search, SEO optimization, and display.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.value`. Unique per-snapshot.

sequence.description:
Display order for the tag among multiple tags for a sale snapshot. Controls front-end tag rendering order. Lower sequence appears earlier. 

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.sequence`.

Timestamp of tag record creation.

Reference: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.created_at`.

Represents all properties required to insert a new sale snapshot tag entity per business rules. Upon creation, sequence ordering and uniqueness of tag for a snapshot are enforced. 

References: shopping_sale_snapshot_tags Prisma table.

Creation is restricted to authorized actors (seller/admin), and value/sequence are mandatory.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
ID of the sale snapshot to associate the new tag with. Must reference valid snapshot record.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.shopping_sale_snapshot_id`.

value.description:
Text/tag for search/SEO/categorization. Required and must be unique within snapshot context.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.value`.

sequence.description:
Display order among all tags for the snapshot. Lower number = higher priority.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.sequence`.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotTag.description:
Alias/entity view for the sale snapshot tag returned by POST/PUT/GET endpoints on snapshot tag management routes for shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.

Expanded object view for the tag, including all relational and metadata context relevant for tag management and display in the admin/customer UI.

Refer to ISaleSnapshotTag for full property contract, as all properties are mirrored in this alias.

References: Prisma table shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.

To maintain separation of DTO duties, this type exists as a semantic alias; may be extended with additional relations if required.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotTag.IUpdate.description:

Permits editing tag value (keyword/text), sequence order, or both. Patchable for allowing targeted field replacement in admin/seller interfaces.

All updates validated for uniqueness (tag value) and correct ordering.

IShoppingCart.description:
Shopping cart entity model for the e-commerce shopping mall system.

Embodies all key properties of a logical cart for a specific connection (customer/seller/admin actor), as described in the shopping_carts table. Used in shopping cart management, coursework, checkout, and analytics APIs. 

Maps directly to Prisma table shopping_carts. 

All cart entity properties include base identification, ownership/customer, actor, time, and relation status, as well as core relations that determine cart item (commodity) composition.

Due to security and audit/evidence requirements, "deleted" is soft, preserving records for investigation/logging.

Entity serves for both direct cart display and data integration in deeper workflows.

id.description:
Primary key, unique identifier for cart. 

Reference: `shopping_carts.id`.

shopping_customer_id.description:
FK to the customer/connection associated with this cart record. Allows multi-cart analytics and security traceability.

Reference: `shopping_carts.shopping_customer_id`.

deleted_at.description: If set, indicates date/time of logical deletion/expiration. Cart is preserved for historic trace but not usable for active checkout.

Used by customer/seller/admin to initialize a new cart session per the shopping_carts business rules. Upon creation, cart is linked to the initiating actor as a new, empty, or optionally pre-filled structure.

Fields must conform to Prisma model for insertable properties.

Security: Only authorized actors may create valid carts—and only one active cart per context is typically allowed policy.

References: Prisma table shopping_carts.

Only permitted mutable fields are included (as per business requirements and evidence policy). Security validation restricts to genuine owner or privileged actor. Cannot update fields critical to relational or audit-trace context.

References: shopping_carts Prisma table.
Possible fields: logical deletion, actor type (if business allows), session-related meta.

Update scenarios may include marking deleted (soft delete), changing actor role (if admin-permitted), or restoring expired carts for analysis or testing.

IShoppingCartCommodity.description:
Commodity (item) record in a shopping cart, referencing a sale snapshot for checkout with chosen configuration.

Each commodity holds the configuration state for one product as selected by the customer in the cart session (volume, deletion status, published/ordered status, and core relationships for stock configuration).

References: Prisma table shopping_cart_commodities; serves as both a relational and data-rich link between shopping_carts and sale snapshots.

volume.description:

Reference: `shopping_cart_commodities.volume`.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this item was added to the cart.

oneOf.description: Soft-deletion timestamp. If set, item is excluded from active cart computation, retained for audit/evidence.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion timestamp. If set, item is excluded from active cart computation, retained for audit/evidence.

oneOf.description: Optional keyword for searching within donation reasons.

reason_keyword.description: Optional keyword for searching within donation reasons.

oneOf.description: Page number for pagination results (1-based index).

page.description: Page number for pagination results (1-based index).

oneOf.description: Page size for paginated responses (default or max as per system config).

IShoppingMileageDonation.IRequest.description:
Request parameters and filters for listing/searching administrative mileage donation records.

Used in user account portals and administrative audit/report interfaces. Maps to advanced query needs over shopping_mileage_donations.

data.description: Array of paginated donation records.

IPageIShoppingMileageDonation.description:
Paginated container for results of administrative mileage donation transaction records.

Standardizes output for list endpoints, including both results and pagination info. Conforms to IPage<T> design pattern for OpenAPI specifications.

id.description:
Unique identifier for donation record (primary key).

Mapped from Prisma column and immutable for evidence compliance.

shopping_admin_customer_id.description:
Reference to the administrator's customer account (the issuer of the donation).

Directly aligns with shopping_customers.id in the schema.

shopping_citizen_id.description:
Reference to the citizen (recipient) receiving the donation.

Must match an existing shopping_citizens.id.

value.description:
Amount of mileage donated in this transaction.

Strictly validates as positive and non-zero. Referenced as value in the Prisma model.

reason.description:
Business or audit reason for the donation event (e.g., campaign, admin support, promo).

Critical for evidence in client support and campaign analytics.

created_at.description:
Timestamp for when the donation transaction was created in the system.

Supports audit, analytics, and compliance reporting.

IShoppingMileageDonation.description:
Mileage donation transaction record.

Represents a single instance where mileage points were donated to a user by an administrative actor, for reasons including campaigns or support. Maps to shopping_mileage_donations in Prisma. All records are retained for tracing and auditing.

shopping_admin_customer_id.description:
Administrator's customer ID making the donation.

Must match a current shopping_customers.id.

shopping_citizen_id.description:
Recipient citizen ID.

Matches shopping_citizens.id; required for donation attribution.

value.description: Mileage value to be donated (must be positive and non-zero as per DB logic).

reason.description:
Required business reason for donation event, e.g., campaign, compensation, promo.

Incorporates policy rationale and supports later audit.

IShoppingMileageDonation.ICreate.description:
Creation object for initiating a new mileage donation transaction.

Given to administrative panels and workflows. Enforces all business/validation rules as per the schema.

oneOf.description:
Updated mileage value for the donation transaction, if correction is allowed.

Subject to audit and support policies.

value.description:
Updated mileage value for the donation transaction, if correction is allowed.

Subject to audit and support policies.

oneOf.description: Updated or corrected donation reason. Used for administrative annotation or dispute resolution.

reason.description: Updated or corrected donation reason. Used for administrative annotation or dispute resolution.

IShoppingMileageDonation.IUpdate.description:
Updation shape for an existing mileage donation record.

Permits administrative update of mutable fields before transaction is finalized or locked. Conforms to business process for correcting donation records after entry but before external exposure.

success.description: True if deletion was successful (record marked as deleted or removed).

oneOf.description: Optional message or context about the deletion outcome.

message.description: Optional message or context about the deletion outcome.

IDeletionResult.description:
Indicates the result of a delete operation (soft- or hard-delete).

Includes core boolean status, possible user-facing message. Used for all deletion endpoints, especially where business or technical logic may block removal.

oneOf.description: Restrict results by citizen ID (user for whom mileage transaction is logged).

shopping_citizen_id.description: Restrict results by citizen ID (user for whom mileage transaction is logged).

oneOf.description: Restrict results to a specific mileage type/spec (metadata). Used for scenario-based search.

shopping_mileage_id.description: Restrict results to a specific mileage type/spec (metadata). Used for scenario-based search.

oneOf.description: Textual filter for history type or classification (income, outcome, bonus, etc).

type.description: Textual filter for history type or classification (income, outcome, bonus, etc).

oneOf.description: Inclusive 'from' (start) filter by transaction creation date.

from.description: Inclusive 'from' (start) filter by transaction creation date.
