to.description: Exclusive 'to' (end) filter by transaction creation date.

oneOf.description: Page number for pagination (1-indexed).
Maximum entries per page in paginated results.

limit.description: Maximum entries per page in paginated results.

IMileageHistory.IRequest.description:
Search, filter, and paging parameters for listing mileage transaction (history) records.

Supports discovery and analytics use-cases, as well as personal mileage history UIs for users.

data.description: Array of mileage history transaction entries.

IPageIMileageHistory.description:
Paginated response record for mileage transaction (history) queries.

Matches standard API container pattern, used for both search and listing views.

id.description: Unique identifier for the mileage history event (transaction).

shopping_mileage_id.description:
Foreign key to the mileage scenario spec.

Allows classification and source traceability.

shopping_citizen_id.description: Foreign key to the customer/citizen receiving or consuming mileage.

source_id.description:
ID of the business record that triggered the transaction (order, event, etc).

Supports detailed traceability and audit.

value.description: Amount of mileage credited or debited. Always positive in schema; direction is inferred by the 'direction' of mileage spec.

balance.description:
Balance after this transaction was processed.

Snapshotted for audit and reconciliation, as in the schema.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the transaction occurred.

oneOf.description:
Cancellation timestamp; set if transaction was reversed/cancelled (never physically deleted).

Evidence preservation per business and compliance requirements.

cancelled_at.description:
Cancellation timestamp; set if transaction was reversed/cancelled (never physically deleted).

Evidence preservation per business and compliance requirements.

IMileageHistory.description:
Mileage accrual/outcome transaction record for a customer.

Serves as an audit, accounting, and compliance log. Reflects entries in shopping_mileage_histories as per schema, including linked entity references. Supports rich analytics, customer-facing history UI, and audit/compliance use-cases.

limit.description: Records per page (limit for the current search or list operation).

pages.description: Total pages in this result set.

IPage.IPagination.description:
Information block on paginated list responses.

Summarizes pagination state for consumer UI, server, or integration use as described in IPage<T> specification.

IShoppingCartCommodity.IRequest.description:
검색 및 필터 그리고 페이징을 위한 장바구니 상품 요청 데이터 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodities의 레코드를 대량으로 조회할 때 사용되는 필터링 및 옵션 정보를 담고 있으며, 각 필드는 실제 Prisma DB의 shopping_cart_commodities 테이블의 컬럼 또는 그와 연결된 엔티티 특성과 1:1로 매칭되어 상세히 설계되어 있습니다. 이 타입은 프론트엔드와 관리자, 관리자 API 모두에서 고도의 검색 기능 및 대용량 데이터 처리를 위해 사용됩니다.

IPageIShoppingCartCommodity.description:
shopping_cart_commodities 장바구니 상품 페이징 결과 컨테이너 타입입니다.

pagination 필드로 페이지 정보를, data 배열로 실제 장바구니 상품 엔티티 레코드들을 담고 있어, RESTful 검색 결과 및 페이징 처리에서 표준 결과 객체로 사용됩니다. pagination과 data의 내부 타입은 IPage 정책에 따라 설계되어 있습니다.

id.description:
장바구니 커머디티의 기본 키(UUID).

Prisma의 shopping_cart_commodities.id 컬럼 대응. 각 장바구니 아이템의 고유 식별자로 사용됩니다.

shopping_cart_id.description:
소속 장바구니의 ID.

shopping_carts.id를 FK로 참조합니다.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
대상 상품 스냅샷의 ID.

shopping_sale_snapshots.id를 FK로 참조합니다.

volume.description:
장바구니 커머디티에 담긴 수량.

단위: 세트(구성상품 기준), 1 이상의 자연수입니다.

created_at.description:
장바구니 커머디티 상품 생성 시각.

Prisma의 created_at 컬럼에 해당합니다.

oneOf.description: 소프트 삭제 시점. 실제 삭제 대신 논리삭제로 관리합니다.

deleted_at.description: 소프트 삭제 시점. 실제 삭제 대신 논리삭제로 관리합니다.

published.description:
이 상품이 주문으로 전환되었는지 여부를 나타냅니다.

주문화 시 true로 설정되며, 주문 전에는 false입니다.

IShoppingCartCommodity.description:
쇼핑몰 장바구니 내 개별 상품(커머디티) 정보의 전체 레코드를 표현하는 타입입니다.

Prisma shopping_cart_commodities 테이블의 실제 DB 컬럼과 1:1로 매칭되며, 기본 키(id), 장바구니 참조, 판매스냅샷 참조, 수량(volume), 생성일시, 삭제일시, 주문변환여부(published) 등이 존재합니다. 또한 관련 엔티티인 stock, order_goods 배열 등도 구조에 포함합니다. 본 타입은 주문 전 상품구성, 장바구니 내 다양한 아이템, 옵션, 스냅샷 기반 증거 데이터 관리 등 e커머스 업무 도메인의 핵심을 나타냅니다.

shopping_cart_id.description: 대상 장바구니의 ID. 반드시 존재하는 shopping_carts.id를 참조해야 합니다.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description: 담을 상품(판매스냅샷)의 ID.

volume.description: 장바구니에 추가할 상품의 수량(1 이상 자연수).

IShoppingCartCommodity.ICreate.description:
새로운 장바구니 상품(커머디티) 추가 시 요청에 사용되는 데이터 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodities에 신규 아이템을 추가할 때 요구되는 필수/선택 필드(장바구니ID, 스냅샷ID, 수량)를 담으며, 실제 엔티티의 컬럼 및 업무 정책을 충실히 반영하였습니다. 입력 검증, 참조 무결성 확인 등 백엔드 비즈니스 로직에 연계됩니다.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description: 변경할 경우 새로운 상품 스냅샷 ID.

volume.description: 수량 변경 시 새 값(1 이상 자연수).

IShoppingCartCommodity.IUpdate.description:
장바구니 상품(커머디티) 정보 변경 시 사용되는 요청 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodities 엔티티의 수량, 스냅샷 참조, 상태 변경 등 수정 가능한 컬럼들의 변경을 이 타입을 통해 전달합니다. 변경 가능한 필드만 선택적으로 전달되며, 미전달 시 기존값 유지 정책입니다. 프론트엔드, 앱, 관리자 모두에서 공통 활용합니다.

IShoppingCartCommodityStock.IRequest.description:
장바구니 커머디티-개별 유닛 스톡 정보 조회 및 검색을 위한 요청 데이터 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodity_stocks 테이블의 개별 상품유닛-재고 정보 목록을 검색할 때, 장바구니 커머디티 ID, 유닛ID, 스톡ID, 수량, 시퀀스 등 상세 필터조건을 포함하며, 대량 검색, 관리자 진단, 분석, 통계 처리에 폭넓게 쓰입니다.

IPageIShoppingCartCommodityStock.description:
장바구니 커머디티-개별유닛재고 리스트 페이징 컨테이너 타입입니다.

IPage 정책에 따라 페이지네이션(pagination) 정보와 배열(data)을 포함하여, 장바구니 내 옵션/유닛별 재고 정보 다건 검색 및 페이징 구현에서 표준적으로 사용됩니다.

id.description:
장바구니 커머디티-유닛재고 기본키(UUID).

shopping_cart_commodity_stocks.id 컬럼 1:1 대응.

quantity.description: 구매(주문/커머디티) 시 속한 유닛-스톡의 개수(재고, 1 이상).

sequence.description: 장바구니 커머디티 내 옵션, 유닛, 스톡 순번.

IShoppingCartCommodityStock.description:
장바구니 내 개별 상품유닛/재고 단위 정보를 담는 대표 엔티티 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodity_stocks 테이블 컬럼(커머디티 참조, 유닛 참조, 스톡 참조, 수량, 시퀀스 등)과 직접 매핑되며, 실제 장바구니 옵션선택, 수량관리, 유닛단위 연산 및 추적에 사용됩니다. 장바구니-주문, 옵션변경, 마이그레이션 등 광범위한 업무에서 중요한 역할을 합니다.

sequence.description: 해당 커머디티 내부 위치를 위한 순서값.

IShoppingCartCommodityStock.ICreate.description:
장바구니 커머디티 내 개별 유닛/재고 신규 추가 요청 데이터 타입입니다.

커머디티-개별유닛 스톡 신규 레코드 생성(상품유닛 및 스톡참조, 수량 등) 시 활용되며, 입력 검증, 중복체크, 수량정책 등 백엔드 비즈니스 로직과 연동됩니다.

sequence.description: 커머디티 내부 순서값 조정.

IShoppingCartCommodityStock.IUpdate.description:
장바구니 커머디티-유닛 스톡 정보 수정 요청 타입입니다.

커머디티 내 특정 옵션, 유닛-스톡 단위 수량/시퀀스 등의 변경작업을 위한 데이터 구조로, 선택적 필드 업데이트 방식을 따릅니다. 미전달값은 기존 데이터 유지 정책이며, 관리자/사용자/앱 공용으로 활용합니다.

IShoppingCartCommodityStockChoice.IReque.description:
장바구니 커머디티 스톡 옵션 선택 정보 목록 조회 및 검색 요청 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodity_stock_choices 엔티티의 대량 옵션선택 이력 및 설정 정보를 페이징, 필터링, 옵션ID, 후보ID 등으로 유연하게 검색할 수 있도록 설계되었습니다.

IPageIShoppingCartCommodityStockChoice.description:
장바구니 커머디티 옵션선택정보(choices) 페이징 결과 컨테이너입니다.

pagination 필드로 페이징 정보를, data 배열로 실제 옵션선택 엔티티 목록을 담아 API, 관리자, 통계 등 다양한 검색 UX에서 표준처럼 쓰입니다.

id.description: 장바구니 커머디티-스톡-옵션선택ID. 기본키 UUID.

oneOf.description: 옵션이 'select' 타입일 때 선택된 후보ID. 아닐 경우 null.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_option_candi.description: 옵션이 'select' 타입일 때 선택된 후보ID. 아닐 경우 null.

oneOf.description: 옵션이 서술형(string, number, boolean 등)일 때는 value에 사용자가 입력 또는 선택한 값 저장. select 타입인 경우 null.

value.description: 옵션이 서술형(string, number, boolean 등)일 때는 value에 사용자가 입력 또는 선택한 값 저장. select 타입인 경우 null.

sequence.description: 소속 커머디티 스톡 내 해당 옵션선택의 순번. 옵션그룹 순번에 대응.

IShoppingCartCommodityStockChoice.description:
장바구니 아이템 내 개별 스톡-옵션선택 정보를 담는 엔티티 타입.

shopping_cart_commodity_stock_choices 테이블 구조(옵션 레퍼런스, 후보ID/value, 시퀀스 등)와 1:1 매칭. 상품유닛 옵션 선택, 커머디티 구성 변경, DB검증 로직에 활용됩니다.

limit.description:
페이지당 레코드 수.

기본값 100.

pages.description: 전체 페이지 수 (마지막 페이지: records/limit의 올림값).

IPage.IPagination.description:
API 페이지네이션을 위한 표준 페이징 정보.

current(현재 페이지), limit(1페이지 크기), records(전체건수), pages(총페이지)로 구성되어 다양한 페이지 처리 시 정형화된 결과 응답에 필수로 포함됩니다.

name: build
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'test/**'
      - 'package.json'
jobs:
  Ubuntu:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20.x
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 8
      
      - name: Install Backend-Server
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build Swagger
        run: npm run build:swagger

      - name: Build SDK
        run: npm run build:sdk

      - name: Compile Backend-Server
        run: npm run build

      - name: Run Test Program
        run: npm run test -- --simultaneous 16

      - name: EsLint
        run: npm run eslint

# Nestia Template
## Outline
[![Build Status](https://github.com/samchon/nestia-start/workflows/build/badge.svg)](https://github.com/samchon/nestia-start/actions?query=workflow%3Abuild)

A template repository for backend projects using [nestia](https://github.com/samchon/nestia).

You can create a new project from this boilerplate by running below command:

```bash
npx nestia start <directory>
```

For reference, this is a minimal boilerplate project concentrating only on [nestia](https://github.com/samchon/nestia) SDK generation. 

If you wanna much detailed boilerplate project, visit [`@samchon/backend`](https://github.com/samchon/backend).




## Directories and Files
This template project has categorized directories like below.

As you can see from the below, all of the Backend source files are placed into the [src](src/) directory. When you build the TypeScript source files, compiled files would be placed into the `lib` directory following the [tsconfig.json](tsconfig.json) configuration. Otherwise you build client [SDK](#32-sdk) library for npm publishing and their compiled files would be placed into the [packages](packages) directory.

  - [packages/api/](packages/api): SDK module built by `npm run build:api`
  - [src/](src): Backend source directory
    - [src/api/](src/api/): Client SDK that would be published to the `@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api`
      - [**src/api/functional/**](src/api/functional/): API functions generated by the [`nestia`](https://github.com/samchon/nestia)
      - [**src/api/structures/**](src/api/structures/): DTO structures
    - [src/controllers/](src/controllers/): Controller classes of the Main Program
  - [**test/**](test): Test Automation Program
  - [nestia.config.ts](nestia.config.ts): Configuration file of [`nestia`](https://github.com/samchon/nestia)
  - [package.json](package.json): NPM configuration
  - [tsconfig.json](tsconfig.json): TypeScript configuration for the main program




## NPM Run Commands
List of the run commands defined in the [package.json](package.json) are like below:

  - Test
    - **`test`**: Run test automation program
    - `benchmark`: Run performance benchmark program
  - Build
    - `build`: Build everything
    - `build:main`: Build main program (`src` directory)
    - `build:test` Build test automation program (`test` directory)
    - `build:sdk`: Build SDK into main program only
    - `build:swagger`: Build Swagger Documents
    - **`dev`**: Incremental build for development (test program)
  - Deploy
    - `package:api`: Build and deploy the SDK library to the NPM
    - `start`: Start the backend server
    - `start:dev`: Start the backend server with incremental build and reload
  - Webpack
    - `webpack`: Run webpack bundler
    - `webpack:start`: Start the backend server built by webpack
    - `webpack:test`: Run test program to the webpack built




## Specialization
Transform this template project to be yours.

When you've created a new backend project through this template project, you can specialize it to be suitable for you by changing some words. Replace below words through IDE specific function like `Edit > Replace in Files` (*Ctrl + Shift + H*), who've been supported by the VSCode.

| Before          | After
|-----------------|----------------------------------------
| ORGANIZATION | Your account or corporation name
| PROJECT      | Your own project name
| AUTHOR       | Author name
| https://github.com/samchon/nestia-start | Your repository URL




## Test Driven Development
With [nestia](https://github.com/samchon/nestia) helps to accomplish TDD (Test Driven Development). 

Just define DTOs and API controllers' methods (only declarations) first. After the definitions, and build SDK (Software Development Kit) through [nestia](https://github.com/samchon/nestia) (`npm run build:sdk`). After buildling those SDK, develop test automation program using the SDK, following use-case scenarios in the framework of client side.

During the test automation program development, you can find that which API is miss-designed or which requirement analysis is not exact. Development of the main program must be the last step after such validation process during TDD.

> Visit the [samchon/backend](https://github.com/samchon/backend), then you may find much detailed story about this TDD.
>
> 1. Definitions
> 2. SDK
> 3. Test Automation Program
> 4. Main Program

```typescript
import {
  ArrayUtil,
  GaffComparator,
  RandomGenerator,
  TestValidator,
} from "@nestia/e2e";

import api from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/index";
import { IBbsArticle } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/bbs/IBbsArticle";
import { IPage } from "@ORGANIZATION/PROJECT-api/lib/structures/common/IPage";

export async function test_api_bbs_article_index_sort(
  connection: api.IConnection,
): Promise<void> {
  // GENERATE 100 ARTICLES
  const section: string = "general";
  await ArrayUtil.asyncRepeat(100)(() =>
    api.functional.bbs.articles.create(connection, section, {
      writer: RandomGenerator.name(),
      title: RandomGenerator.paragraph(5)(),
      body: RandomGenerator.content(8)()(),
      format: "txt",
      files: [],
      password: RandomGenerator.alphabets(8),
    }),
  );

  // PREPARE VALIDATOR
  const validator = TestValidator.sort("BbsArticleProvider.index()")(async (
    sort: IPage.Sort<IBbsArticle.IRequest.SortableColumns>,
  ) => {
    const page: IPage<IBbsArticle.ISummary> =
      await api.functional.bbs.articles.index(connection, section, {
        limit: 100,
        sort,
      });
    return page.data;
  });

  // DO VALIDATE
  const components = [
    validator("created_at")(GaffComparator.dates((x) => x.created_at)),
    validator("updated_at")(GaffComparator.dates((x) => x.updated_at)),
    validator("title")(GaffComparator.strings((x) => x.title)),
    validator("writer")(GaffComparator.strings((x) => x.writer)),
    validator(
      "writer",
      "title",
    )(GaffComparator.strings((x) => [x.writer, x.title])),
  ];
  for (const comp of components) {
    await comp("+", false);
    await comp("-", false);
  }
}
```

For reference, if you run `npm run benchmark` command, your test functions defined in the [test/features/api](test/features/api) directory would be utilized for performance benchmarking. If you want to see the performance bench result earlier, visit below link please:

  - [docs/benchmarks/AMD Ryzen 9 7940HS w Radeon 780M Graphics.md](https://github.com/samchon/nestia-start/blob/master/docs/benchmarks/AMD%20Ryzen%209%207940HS%20w%20Radeon%20780M%20Graphics.md)

# SDK Library
This is a SDK library generated by [`nestia`](https://nestia.io).

With this SDK library, you can easily and safely interact with backend server.

Just import and call some API functions like gif image below:

![nestia-sdk-demo](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13158709/215004990-368c589d-7101-404e-b81b-fbc936382f05.gif)

> Left is server code, and right is client code utilizing the SDK




# What [`Nestia`](https://nestia.io) is:
![Nestia Logo](https://nestia.io/logo.png)

[![GitHub license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://github.com/samchon/nestia/blob/master/LICENSE)
[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@nestia/core.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nestia/core)
[![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/@nestia/core.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nestia/core)
[![Build Status](https://github.com/samchon/nestia/workflows/build/badge.svg)](https://github.com/samchon/nestia/actions?query=workflow%3Abuild)
[![Guide Documents](https://img.shields.io/badge/guide-documents-forestgreen)](https://nestia.io/docs/)

Nestia is a set of helper libraries for NestJS, supporting below features:

  - `@nestia/core`: super-fast decorators
  - `@nestia/sdk`:
    - Swagger generator evolved than ever
    - SDK library generator for clients
    - Mockup Simulator for client applications
    - Automatic E2E test functions generator
  - `@nestia/migrate`: migration from Swagger to NestJS
  - `nestia`: just CLI (command line interface) tool

> **Note**
> 
> - **Only one line** required, with pure TypeScript type
> - Enhance performance **30x** up
>   - Runtime validator is **20,000x faster** than `class-validator`
>   - JSON serialization is **200x faster** than `class-transformer`
> - Software Development Kit
>   - SDK is a collection of `fetch` functions with type definitions like [tRPC](https://trpc.io/)
>   - Mockup simulator means embedded backend simulator in SDK
>     - similar with [msw](https://mswjs.io/), but fully automated

import { tags } from "typia";

export namespace IShoppingSaleSnapshotInquiryComment {
  /**
   * Request payload for updating an inquiry comment in
   * `shopping_sale_snapshot_inquiry_comments` (a subtype of
   * `bbs_article_comments`).
   *
   * This schema is for modifying the content, format, or parent relationship
   * of a comment attached to a sale snapshot inquiry. Each update results in
   * a new snapshot for evidentiary purposes.
   *
   * Follows the evidence-preserving design in the shopping mall system and is
   * compliant with all relevant business and legal audit requirements.
   */
  export type IUpdate = {
    /**
     * The updated content of the inquiry comment.
     *
     * Refers to the `body` field of `bbs_article_comment_snapshots` in the
     * Prisma schema. Contains the main textual data for the comment
     * update.
     *
     * According to the schema, a new snapshot is created for the content
     * modifications rather than altering the original comment, supporting
     * audit trails and evidence preservation.
     */
    body: string;

    /**
     * Format of the comment body (e.g., 'html', 'md', 'txt').
     *
     * References the `format` field in `bbs_article_comment_snapshots`,
     * indicating the content type the comment is written in. This allows
     * correct rendering on the frontend and proper audit for historical
     * revisions.
     *
     * Supplying this ensures that the format is accounted for when a new
     * snapshot is made, as per evidence-compliance requirements.
     */

     * reply.
     *
     * References the `parent_id` column in `bbs_article_comments` in the

     * enabling replies to other comments. May be null if updating a
     * top-level comment.

    parent_id?: string & tags.Format<"uuid">;
  };

Deleting a category is an irreversible action and must be handled with care, given its place in the hierarchy. When a category is deleted, all child categories should either be reassigned or removed according to business rules to preserve referential integrity.

It is important to verify that there are no dependent sales, products, or subcategories before deletion. Security context should ensure only privileged users (e.g., administrators) may perform this operation. Error handling should include detection of existing dependencies (such as associated products or child categories) and respond with appropriate error messages if deletion cannot proceed immediately.

Related endpoints include PATCH (for searching/listing all channel categories), POST (for creating), GET (for retrieving details), and PUT (for updating).

Administrators in this system are members who have been granted elevated privileges to manage system-wide settings, roles, and audit logs, as described in the 'shopping_administrators' table. The list can include both active and withdrawn administrators for auditing and record-keeping purposes.

This endpoint is crucial for system management, allowing oversight of all individuals with administrative access. Security is a primary concern; only users with appropriate permissions should be allowed to access this list. The operation enforces access controls as per system policy.

Related operations include endpoints for creating (/post), retrieving details (/get), updating (/put), and deleting (/delete) specific administrators. Validation for filtering, pagination, and search parameters must follow best practices to avoid injection issues and ensure efficient query performance. Any errors should return clear, actionable messages, especially with respect to permissions or invalid query combinations.
operations.description:
The list administrators endpoint offers a comprehensive, paginated view of system administrators based on the 'shopping_administrators' Prisma schema. According to schema comments, each administrator is a member elevated to admin status and associated with a unique 'shopping_members' record. The operation enables filtering by creation date, status (withdrawn/active), and member relationship. Admins are critical to controlling sensitive resources and operations— thus, role-based access controls must be strictly enforced. 

Pagination, search, and sorting parameters are supported to allow large sets of administrators to be explored efficiently. Error handling ensures only authorized users can access this endpoint, and improper parameters lead to descriptive errors. The result returns administrator summaries, supporting audit and management processes. Related endpoints include those for creation, detail retrieval, update, and removal of administrator records.

Access to this endpoint typically requires system-level permissions, and audit trails should be logged for all requests, as per comments in the underlying DB schema.

Each administrator is tied to a unique member (shopping_members.id). This endpoint is used to view the complete profile, status, permissions, and record history of a specific administrator for management and auditing.

Access to this route must be restricted to users with adequate authorization. The response provides all properties available on the administrator entity, including relations to member and audit trails where applicable. Care must be taken to validate the provided {id} is a valid administrator identifier. Errors from missing records or insufficient permissions are clearly communicated back to the client.

This operation is often used in conjunction with the list, create, update, and delete endpoints for administrators. It supports system management, role assignment, and audit tracking by exposing robust administrator detail information.

The get administrator detail endpoint returns the complete profile of a single administrator as defined in the 'shopping_administrators' Prisma table. Associated member data, current status (active/withdrawn), and historical records are included per the schema comments. As administrators have full or partial system control, only users with the appropriate permissions are authorized to access this detail.

Validation ensures the provided ID is well-formed and exists in the database. Detailed error messages help in diagnosing not found or permission errors. Logging of access is strongly advised to comply with audit and accountability requirements. This endpoint supports user management, permission reviews, and system oversight functions.

The administrator is associated with a shopping_members record, and is granted administrative privileges as specified in system policy.

Upon creation, validation checks ensure the member exists, is not already an administrator, and meets any eligibility criteria (such as authenticity verification). The endpoint logs the creation event for audit purposes. It is used by other administrators or system superusers to expand admin staff.

Only users with high-level permissions should be permitted to perform this operation, and all actions must be properly logged. Errors (such as attempting to promote an already-admin user) are returned with clear diagnostics.

Security checks confirm the member's eligibility (membership, verification, not previously withdrawn, etc.) before assignment. All administrator creation events are recorded for auditing. Upon success, the new administrator's full detail is returned.

If a member cannot be promoted (e.g., already withdrawn or already an admin), an error is provided. Related operations support listing, details, updating, and removal of administrators. Strict access control and event logging are enforced throughout the process.

Access must be restricted by roles— administrators may view all, while customers see only their own. The result includes address details, creation timestamps, and any associated metadata. This endpoint is core to both user account management and logistics/fulfillment workflows.

The list operation supports search, filter, and sorting for key fields— status, date, section, seller, etc. It also strictly enforces access control: sellers see their products, administrators can see all, and customers access only public/open sales. The operation does not directly include sale snapshot information — after registration, sellers must use subsequent endpoints to define detailed item configuration, pricing, product options, or content. If the provided section or seller information is invalid, the system responds with an error. This operation is transactional: if any part of the creation process fails, the entire creation is rolled back. The endpoint is designed for extensibility to allow bulk operations later, but initially supports a single-object creation per request.

Nullable reference for hierarchical reply/comment threading, mapping to parent bbs_article_comments.id.

Allows for multi-level discussion and reply chains; can be omitted for root level comments.

parent_id.description:
Nullable reference for hierarchical reply/comment threading, mapping to parent bbs_article_comments.id.

Allows for multi-level discussion and reply chains; can be omitted for root level comments.

created_at.description:
Timestamp (ISO 8601 with timezone) when the comment was created as required by evidence preservation policy.

Mapped from Prisma schema, used for ordering and audit.

oneOf.description:
Nullable timestamp marking comment as soft-deleted. Instead of removing, this field is set to preserve audit trail and legal evidence per shopping mall policy.

Corresponds to Prisma bbs_article_comments.deleted_at.

deleted_at.description:
Nullable timestamp marking comment as soft-deleted. Instead of removing, this field is set to preserve audit trail and legal evidence per shopping mall policy.

Corresponds to Prisma bbs_article_comments.deleted_at.

snapshots.description:
Snapshots of the comment content, maintained for historical edit tracking and evidence. New version (snapshot) is created on every edit per system policy.

Maps to bbs_article_comment_snapshots in the DB.

children.description: List of child comments (replies), implementing the recursive reply tree as described in the schema.

IBbsArticleComment.description:
Represents a comment on a bulletin board article (Prisma model bbs_article_comments).

Includes audit and evidence preservation features as in the shopping mall system DB design: all values are evidence-locked, and even deletions preserve the comment state. Tracks all modification histories, supports threaded replies, and models soft-delete with deleted_at.

body.description:
The main text/content body of the comment as submitted by the user at creation time.

Required as per comment creation process; stored in a new snapshot for evidence.

format.description:
Format of the comment body (e.g., 'html', 'md', 'txt'), copied from bbs_article_comment_snapshots.format.

Default determined by client/editor; required by schema.

oneOf.description:
Optional parent comment ID if this comment is a reply to another comment (enables threaded discussions).

Nullable; required for reply scenarios, otherwise omitted.

parent_id.description:
Optional parent comment ID if this comment is a reply to another comment (enables threaded discussions).

Nullable; required for reply scenarios, otherwise omitted.

IBbsArticleComment.ICreate.description:
Request body for creating a new comment on a bulletin board article.

Requires comment body and format for evidence and content storage. Parent_id is needed only for replies in threaded view.

body.description:
New value for the comment body after editing (required for update).

Stored in a new snapshot preserving modification history for legal evidence compliance.

format.description: Format of the updated comment body (copied to snapshot as in IBbsArticleComment.ICreate).

IBbsArticleComment.IUpdate.description:
Request body schema for updating a board comment.

Both body and format must be supplied; each update results in a new snapshot to preserve edit trails.

id.description:
Primary key for the comment snapshot as per Prisma bbs_article_comment_snapshots.id.

Uniquely identifies each edit/version of a comment.

format.description: Format of the comment body (e.g., 'html', 'md', 'txt'). Linked to format field in parent comment or editor choice.

body.description: Comment body/content at the time of this snapshot (immutable after creation for evidence).

created_at.description: Timestamp of when this snapshot/version was created. Used for auditing and evidence.

files.description: List of file attachments (if any) at this version. Persists evidence for comment edits/revisions.

IBbsArticleCommentSnapshot.description:
Represents a snapshot (version) of a comment as per shopping mall audit requirements (Prisma bbs_article_comment_snapshots).

Each edit to a comment generates a new instance of this type for full evidence, forensic, and audit coverage.

id.description:
Primary key of the attachment file. Unique UUID assigned to each uploaded file in the shopping mall system.

Persistent identifier for tracing file usage across DB and snapshot references.

name.description: Storage name of the file (excluding extension). Empty for dotfiles (e.g., '.gitignore') but not both name and extension empty.

oneOf.description: File extension (nullable); e.g., 'jpg', 'pdf', or null for extensionless files.

extension.description: File extension (nullable); e.g., 'jpg', 'pdf', or null for extensionless files.

url.description:
URL or storage path to the real file asset (DB field: url). Required, up to 1024 characters.

Used to retrieve or present the actual file in client and admin panels.

created_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601) of file upload/storing event. Used for audit, ordering, and historical reference.

IAttachmentFile.description:
Metadata representation of an attachment file from the Prisma attachment_files table.

Files may be referenced by articles, comments, or product/sale information; used for evidence, legal, and audit purposes. Stores all metadata but not the physical asset.

code.description: Optional filtering to a specific channel code; unique per channel in the system.

Filter to include only active or soft-deleted channels ('deleted_at' null / non-null, mapped to enum here).

limit.description: Number of records per page (page size).

records.description: Total number of records across all pages.

IPage.IPagination.description: Page information for paginated API responses. Apply across all 'IPage<T>' containers to describe result metadata.

id.description: Unique identifier for the channel, assigned at creation (DB field: shopping_channels.id).

code.description: Code name for the channel, e.g., 'web', 'app2'. Must be unique per channel as per DB schema.

name.description: Human-friendly channel display name; must be unique per channel as per schema.

created_at.description: Time of channel creation (UTC, ISO 8601).

updated_at.description: Time of last update to channel configuration. Required for database consistency and audit.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp for compliance with evidence retention. Set when channel is deleted/removed, otherwise null.

IShoppingChannel.description:
Represents a full channel entity in the shopping mall system, as described by the shopping_channels Prisma model.

Contains audit fields such as created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at, plus business identifiers code and name with uniqueness requirements.

code.description: Unique code for the new channel; domain/business-meaningful and enforced as unique at the DB layer.

name.description: Display name for the new channel; must be unique among all channels.

IShoppingChannel.ICreate.description: Request body required for creating a new shopping mall channel. Enforces unique code and name values. Timestamp fields are set by the backend.

code.description: (Optional) Code to update the channel's code (must remain unique if provided).

name.description: (Optional) New channel display name (must remain unique as per DB constraint).

oneOf.description: Optionally set the channel as soft-deleted or restore by updating the timestamp.

deleted_at.description: Optionally set the channel as soft-deleted or restore by updating the timestamp.

IShoppingChannel.IUpdate.description: Request body for updating a channel entity (shopping_channels). All fields optional; system logic enforces proper uniqueness and audit consistency.

channel_id.description: Optional, filter categories for specific channel by channel id.

oneOf.description:
Optional, filter by specific parent category (to get subcategories in hierarchy).

Nullable for root categories search.

parent_id.description:
Optional, filter by specific parent category (to get subcategories in hierarchy).

Nullable for root categories search.

code.description: Category code (string match, supports search and filtering).

name.description: Category name (supports partial and full match for search).

oneOf.description: State: only active or only soft-deleted categories. Maps to deleted_at presence in Prisma.
State: only active or only soft-deleted categories. Maps to deleted_at presence in Prisma.

status.description: State: only active or only soft-deleted categories. Maps to deleted_at presence in Prisma.

IShoppingChannelCategory.IRequest.description:
Query parameters for searching, filtering, and paginating channel category lists.

Maps fields from the shopping_channel_categories Prisma schema and indexes.

IPageIShoppingChannelCategory.ISummary.description: Paginated result container for channel category summaries (

IShoppingChannelCategory.ISummary.description: Channel category summary object for paged lists, lookups, hierarchical browser displays. Contains identification and minimal navigation info.

oneOf.description:
Optional reference to the parent category for hierarchy/view trees.

Null for top-level categories.

parent_id.description:
Optional reference to the parent category for hierarchy/view trees.

Null for top-level categories.

name.description: Display name for the category. Unique only within parent/channel for flexible hierarchies.

code.description: Unique string identifier for the category in the context of the channel.

updated_at.description: Last updated timestamp, maintained for category moves/renames.

oneOf.description: Soft delete timestamp as required for audit and evidence retention.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp as required for audit and evidence retention.

IShoppingChannelCategory.description:
Complete representation of a shopping_channel_categories entity as per DB schema.

Includes parent, code, name, and timestamps for audit and navigation.

channel_id.description: Channel reference under which to create the category (required; checked for existence).

oneOf.description: Parent category ID for hierarchical tree (nullable for root nodes).

name.description: Name for the new category (must be unique within channel/parent).

IShoppingChannelCategory.ICreate.description: Request body for creating a new channel category in shopping mall schema. Includes references, business names, and navigation fields.

IPageIShoppingSale.description:
A paginated list of product sales in the shopping mall.

Follows the IPage<T> pattern designed for scalable APIs where product sales are listed with page information for efficient UI navigation. The 'data' array consists of IShoppingSale objects representing individual product sales, while 'pagination' supplies current page, record counts, and page boundaries.

See the original IPage<T> comment for further information on usage and pagination fields.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for the product sale record.

References shopping_sales.id in the Prisma schema.

shopping_section_id.description:
ID of the section (spatial area/corner) this sale belongs to.

References shopping_sections.id in the Prisma schema.

shopping_seller_customer_id.description:
ID of the seller's customer record who owns this sale listing.

References shopping_customers.id in the Prisma schema.

created_at.description:
Creation time of the sale record.

References shopping_sales.created_at in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
Opening time of the sale. If null, not open yet.

References shopping_sales.opened_at from the Prisma schema.

opened_at.description:
Opening time of the sale. If null, not open yet.

References shopping_sales.opened_at from the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
Closing time of the sale. Null if the sale is perpetual.

References shopping_sales.closed_at from the Prisma schema.

closed_at.description:
Closing time of the sale. Null if the sale is perpetual.

References shopping_sales.closed_at from the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
Time when seller paused the sale for any reason.

References shopping_sales.paused_at from the Prisma schema.

paused_at.description:
Time when seller paused the sale for any reason.

References shopping_sales.paused_at from the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
Timestamp when the sale was suspended by the seller or the system.

References shopping_sales.suspended_at from the Prisma schema.

suspended_at.description:
Timestamp when the sale was suspended by the seller or the system.

References shopping_sales.suspended_at from the Prisma schema.

IShoppingSale.description:
Represents a single product sale entry registered by a seller.

The core sale record captures the linkage between sellers and market spatial sections, along with status tracking for open, closed, paused, and suspended sales. Detailed product content, pricing, and configuration are handled through related snapshot and subordinate entities.

All fields below are mapped and documented with attention to their corresponding Prisma schema columns for evidence preservation and traceability in legal or business contexts.

shopping_section_id.description:
ID of the section (market area) this sale is registered in.

This is a required field during sale creation.

References shopping_sections.id from the Prisma schema.

shopping_seller_customer_id.description:
ID of the seller's customer record for this sale listing.

References shopping_customers.id from the Prisma schema. Required to assign the ownership of the sale record to a specific seller.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Opening time for this sale. If omitted or null, the sale is not currently open and requires later activation by the seller or general process.

References shopping_sales.opened_at in Prisma.

opened_at.description:
(Optional) Opening time for this sale. If omitted or null, the sale is not currently open and requires later activation by the seller or general process.

References shopping_sales.opened_at in Prisma.

IShoppingSale.ICreate.description:
Schema for registering a new product sale by a seller (creation POST operation).

Takes input for spatial section and seller, as well as (optionally) the opening time. The ID and creation timestamp are not client-supplied but are assigned automatically by the backend. Mapped from the shopping_sales model in Prisma.

Required for product sale registration workflows, ensuring valid section/seller linkage upon creation.

shopping_section_id.description:
(Optional) Updated section ID for the product sale listing.

If the product moves to a new spatial section in the mall, this value is supplied here.

References shopping_sections.id in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Update the opening time. Null means unset or not open yet.

References shopping_sales.opened_at in the Prisma schema.

opened_at.description:
(Optional) Update the opening time. Null means unset or not open yet.

References shopping_sales.opened_at in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Update the closing time for the sale, or set null for indefinite.

References shopping_sales.closed_at in Prisma.

closed_at.description:
(Optional) Update the closing time for the sale, or set null for indefinite.

References shopping_sales.closed_at in Prisma.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Update the paused time for this sale.

References shopping_sales.paused_at in the Prisma schema.

paused_at.description:
(Optional) Update the paused time for this sale.

References shopping_sales.paused_at in the Prisma schema.

oneOf.description:
(Optional) Update/inject suspended timestamp for the sale.

Used for marking the sale suspended (manually or automatically per business logic).

References shopping_sales.suspended_at from the Prisma schema.

suspended_at.description:
(Optional) Update/inject suspended timestamp for the sale.

Used for marking the sale suspended (manually or automatically per business logic).

References shopping_sales.suspended_at from the Prisma schema.

IShoppingSale.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating a product sale entry.

All fields are optional—client supplies only those to be updated. This schema covers status transitions of sale records including opening, closing, pausing, and suspending sales. Leveraged by seller/admin update operations mapped to shopping_sales table in Prisma.

Required for sale lifecycle management workflows and audit compliance.

shopping_sale_id.description:
(Optional) Filter by sale ID to retrieve snapshots of a specific sale.

Reference: shopping_sale_snapshots.shopping_sale_id in the Prisma schema.

created_from.description:
(Optional) Filter for snapshots created after this timestamp.

Reference: created_at in shopping_sale_snapshots.

created_to.description:
(Optional) Filter for snapshots created before this timestamp.

Reference: created_at in shopping_sale_snapshots.

limit.description: Maximum number of snapshot records per page (pagination).

IShoppingSaleSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Request structure for searching or listing product sale snapshots.

Includes filters for sale ID and creation timestamp range. Pagination controls are supplied for efficient UI navigation and to handle high-volume snapshot data.

All properties map to fields or query scenarios supported by shopping_sale_snapshots in Prisma, implementing compliance for evidence preservation and audit trails.

IPageShoppingSaleSnapshot.description:
A paginated result list of product sale snapshot records.

Conforms to the IPage<T> interface, with 'data' array containing IShoppingSaleSnapshot entities and 'pagination' field representing current page, counts, and record bounds.

Frequently used in APIs supporting browsing, analysis, or evidence gathering for product configuration histories.

id.description:
Primary key of this sale snapshot record.

References shopping_sale_snapshots.id from Prisma.

shopping_sale_id.description:
ID of parent sale to which this snapshot belongs.

References shopping_sales.id.

created_at.description:
Timestamp of when this snapshot was created.

References shopping_sale_snapshots.created_at.

IShoppingSaleSnapshot.description:
A historical or current configuration snapshot of a product sale.

Contains immutable records for a product's key configuration state at a single moment in time—supporting versioned product details, pricing, and compliance evidence for legal or business reasons. Further details (units, content, etc.) reside in subordinate or related entities as per the Prisma schema.

Each field maps to a corresponding Prisma schema property for reliable cross-reference and audit trail integrity.

shopping_sale_id.description:
Sale ID for which a new snapshot will be produced.

Requirement: must reference a valid existing sale (shopping_sales.id).

Required upon creation.

IShoppingSaleSnapshot.ICreate.description:
Schema for creating a new product sale snapshot record.

Enables sellers/admins to register a new historical version of a sale, fulfilling requirements for evidence, versioning, and auditability in the shopping system. The only field required from client is the sale reference; all other details are managed by related subordinate creation endpoints or automated by the backend.

Directly references shopping_sale_snapshots in Prisma.

IShoppingSaleSnapshot.IUpdate.description:
No fields are directly updatable for product sale snapshot records.

Sale snapshot entries are designed to be immutable for evidence and audit compliance. Any changes must be realized by inserting new snapshots, not updating existing ones. Use this schema for API interface consistency only.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
(Optional) Filter by snapshot ID to narrow results to units of a single product sale snapshot.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.shopping_sale_snapshot_id.

name.description:
(Optional) Filter by the name of the product unit (supports partial matching).

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.name.

primary.description:
(Optional) Filter for required (primary) units.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.primary.

required.description:
(Optional) Filter for whether the unit is required to be chosen in a product configuration.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.required.

limit.description: Page size for pagination.

page.description: Page number for paginated result sets.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.IRequest.description:
Structure for listing or searching product unit records inside sale snapshots.

Fields allow filtering by snapshot, name, or flags for primary/required units. Pagination is enabled and aligned with best practices for scalable search and UI display. Type maps to shopping_sale_snapshot_units and related search fields in Prisma.

IPageShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.description:
Paginated wrapper of product unit records for a snapshot.

Implements the IPage<T> pagination and search interface with an array of IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit objects and pagination metadata. Used for configuration wizards, bulk inventory management, and UI presentation of product bundles/options.

id.description:
Primary key for the product unit in the sale snapshot.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.id in Prisma.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
ID of the sale snapshot this unit belongs to.

References shopping_sale_snapshots.id.

name.description:
Display name of the product unit (e.g., Main Body, Keyboard).

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.name in Prisma.

primary.description:
Indicates if this unit is primary for the configuration (label only).

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.primary flag.

required.description:
Indicates if the unit must be selected for any purchase under this sale snapshot.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.required flag.

sequence.description:
Ordering of this unit within the sale snapshot for presentation or processing purposes.

References shopping_sale_snapshot_units.sequence.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.description:
Describes a single product unit as registered within a specific sale snapshot.

Stores all relevant attributes for bundled goods, product components, or options—label, display, and configuration flags. Each record is associated to a parent snapshot for versioning and audit traceability. All fields trace directly back to columns in the shopping_sale_snapshot_units table for reliable system mapping and legal compliance.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
ID of the sale snapshot ({@link shopping_sale_snapshots.id}) this unit belongs to.

Required to associate the unit with a particular version of a product's configuration. Enforces referential integrity and supports audit and legal traceability.

name.description:
Representative name of the unit in this sale snapshot (e.g., 'Main Body', 'Accessory', 'Apple Care').

Must be unique within the belonging snapshot. As per schema comment, conveys both product display and internal mapping. This title is typically visible in product configuration screens and analytics.

primary.description:
Label indicating if this unit is the most important component among the bundle (primary true/false).

May inform UI display strategies or logic determining purchase flow requirements.

required.description:
Indicates whether it is mandatory for a customer to select this unit as part of the purchase configuration.

Directly supports business rules on product bundling: items like 'Main Body' are required, while 'Accessory' may be optional.

sequence.description:
The ordering number of this unit relative to other units in the same sale snapshot.

Used for explicit product configuration sequence on UI and in the backend, relevant to logical/evidence order in dispute situations.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.ICreate.description: Request body type for creating a sale snapshot unit in the system (shopping_sale_snapshot_units). Represents a component in a product's offered configuration. All properties are required to ensure full provenance, logical ordering, and audit trail alignment as described in the DB schema.

name.description:
Representative name of the unit. Allows edit for display/user context or correction.

Should preserve context, preserve uniqueness if updated.

primary.description:
Whether the unit is considered primary after the update.

Supports dynamic re-labelling of product components post-registration.

required.description:
Flag to adjust whether this unit must be included in a purchase.

May impact validation flows on the customer-facing and admin side.

sequence.description: Update to the sequence/order within the sale snapshot for display/configuration logic.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotUnit.IUpdate.description: Request body type for updating an existing sale snapshot unit. Every property is optional to support PATCH-style partial update semantics. Only permitted fields may be changed, enforcing schema and evidence preservation requirements.

success.description: Indicates whether the delete operation was successful.

message.description: Optional human-readable detail about the result of the delete operation, e.g., reason for failure.

IDeleteResponse.description: Standardized API response type indicating the result of a delete operation. Used for both hard and soft (logical) delete endpoints. Provides success boolean and optional message for diagnostics or UI feedback.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_id.description:
Filter: The parent unit's unique identifier ({@link shopping_sale_snapshot_units.id}).

Allows for retrieving only those options relevant to a specific unit in a sale snapshot. Used for UI configuration, analytics, and tight evidence linking.

type.description:
Filter: Option type. Valid values include: 'select', 'string', 'boolean', 'number'.

May be used to refine results by structural/semantic meaning in product configuration logic.

name.description:
Search/filter: Option name or partial match.

Supports UI searching, admin analytics, or troubleshooting workflows.

page.description: Result page for pagination (1-based index). Default: 1.

limit.description: Number of records per page for pagination. Default: 20 or system preset.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOption.IRequest.description:
Request body for searching and paginating sale snapshot unit options in the system. Input filters allow specification by unit, option type, name (partial/search), and standard pagination options.

Strict parameter validation required, and all searches are audit-logged as per e-commerce system requirements.

data.description: List of sale snapshot unit option summary/domain objects on the returned page.

IPageISaleSnapshotUnitOption.description:
Container type holding a page of ISaleSnapshotUnitOption records, as per system-wide standard paging structure (see IPage<T>). Results are guaranteed to have both high-level pagination details and the current page's data array.

Pagination object per shared IPage spec; data is the slice of requested entities.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the sale snapshot unit option. DB: {@link shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_options.id}

Essential for linking to candidates and evidentiary audit history.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_id.description:
Reference to parent unit. DB: {@link shopping_sale_snapshot_units.id}

Facilitates hierarchical search, display, and integrity enforcement.

name.description:
Display name/title for the option (e.g., 'Color', 'Size').

Business rules may require name uniqueness per unit; supports user UX, analytics, and evidence trails.

type.description:
Type of the option control. Valid values are: 'select' (pick a value), 'string' (free text), 'boolean' (checkbox), 'number' (numeric input).

Directly drives UI rendering and analytics. Schema drives core business logic and evidence policies.

variable.description:
Indicates whether this option is variable (affects final product stock/inventory). See schema for critical conditional logic.

Variable 'select'-type options split stocks; others are metadata.

sequence.description: Order index for displaying options in configuration UI. Also used for evidence order during disputes.

candidates.description: The array of selectable candidate values for this option (only required for 'select'-type options). Preserved for audit, UI, and validation.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOption.description: Response and reference type for an individual sale snapshot unit option in product configuration. Represents one selectable or informational characteristic of a product unit. Candidates field holds possible values for 'select'-type options.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_id.description:
Parent unit in which to create the option. Refers to DB: {@link shopping_sale_snapshot_units.id}

Required for linking and validates existence.

name.description:
Display name for the new option (e.g., 'Color').

Should be unique within the unit to avoid ambiguity, as per schema and business rule specifications.

type.description:
Option type, one of 'select', 'string', 'boolean', 'number'.

Critical attribute for system and UI logic enforcement.

variable.description:
If true, this option will determine inventory/stock splits, permitted only for 'select'-type. Otherwise, it is immaterial for system splitting logic.

Non-variable options are meta only; see schema policy.

sequence.description: Ordering number for UI display and evidence/analytics sequence.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOption.ICreate.description: Create type for a new sale snapshot unit option in the product system. All fields required to ensure entity integrity, unique identification, and correct propagation into evidence/audit chains and the customer UI.

name.description: Update to the option name, affecting UI and analytics but must respect uniqueness per unit.

type.description: Change of option type ('select', 'string', 'boolean', 'number'). Highly regulated; may force backend validation or migration of candidate values.

variable.description: May change if business rules and reference integrity allow. Only meaningful for 'select' type in current spec.

sequence.description: Update to display/order index for option listings.

ISaleSnapshotUnitOption.IUpdate.description: Update schema for sale snapshot unit options. Allows for partial updates (PATCH semantics). Only permitted fields are available, conforming to evidence-preserving schema. Strict backend validation applies.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_option_id.description:
Filter: Parent option to search candidate values for ({@link shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_options.id}).

Enables search, consistency, and efficient UI.

Input type for creating a new tag for a sale snapshot in shopping_sale_snapshot_tags table.

Represents all properties required to insert a new sale snapshot tag entity per business rules. Upon creation, sequence ordering and uniqueness of tag for a snapshot are enforced. 

References: shopping_sale_snapshot_tags Prisma table.

Creation is restricted to authorized actors (seller/admin), and value/sequence are mandatory.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
ID of the sale snapshot to associate the new tag with. Must reference valid snapshot record.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.shopping_sale_snapshot_id`.

value.description:
Text/tag for search/SEO/categorization. Required and must be unique within snapshot context.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.value`.

sequence.description:
Display order among all tags for the snapshot. Lower number = higher priority.

Direct mapping: `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.sequence`.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotTag.description:
Alias/entity view for the sale snapshot tag returned by POST/PUT/GET endpoints on snapshot tag management routes for shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.

Expanded object view for the tag, including all relational and metadata context relevant for tag management and display in the admin/customer UI.

Refer to ISaleSnapshotTag for full property contract, as all properties are mirrored in this alias.

References: Prisma table shopping_sale_snapshot_tags.
Use this type for all entity return scenarios outside requests.

To maintain separation of DTO duties, this type exists as a semantic alias; may be extended with additional relations if required.

IShoppingSaleSnapshotTag.IUpdate.description:
Update (PUT/PATCH) type for sale snapshot tag editing in shopping_sale_snapshot_tags table.

Permits editing tag value (keyword/text), sequence order, or both. Patchable for allowing targeted field replacement in admin/seller interfaces.

All updates validated for uniqueness (tag value) and correct ordering.

References: Prisma `shopping_sale_snapshot_tags`.

Security: restricted to tag's creator/admin role.

value.description: Updated tag keyword/text for SEO/search/product feature management. Must remain unique per sale snapshot context.

sequence.description: Updated order in display/usage sequence among tags for the snapshot. Required if changing tag sorting/priority. Remains unique per snapshot.

IShoppingCart.IRequest.description:

shopping_customer_id.description:

Paginated result structure for shopping cart listing/search results.

Wraps a page of shopping cart records (IShoppingCart) with IPage.IPagination for offset/limit/total analytics for UI, search, and admin context.

Corresponds to PATCH search results endpoints for batch shopping cart analysis.

pagination.description: Pagination metadata for interpreting the current result page in the global context (offset, page, limit, total count, etc).

data.description: Resulting list of shopping cart entities for the current page, each reflecting the IShoppingCart contract for consumer display/interaction.

IShoppingCart.description:
Shopping cart entity model for the e-commerce shopping mall system.

Embodies all key properties of a logical cart for a specific connection (customer/seller/admin actor), as described in the shopping_carts table. Used in shopping cart management, coursework, checkout, and analytics APIs. 

Maps directly to Prisma table shopping_carts. 

All cart entity properties include base identification, ownership/customer, actor, time, and relation status, as well as core relations that determine cart item (commodity) composition.

Due to security and audit/evidence requirements, "deleted" is soft, preserving records for investigation/logging.

Entity serves for both direct cart display and data integration in deeper workflows.

id.description:
Primary key, unique identifier for cart. 

Reference: `shopping_carts.id`.

shopping_customer_id.description:
FK to the customer/connection associated with this cart record. Allows multi-cart analytics and security traceability.

Reference: `shopping_carts.shopping_customer_id`.

oneOf.description:

deleted_at.description: If set, indicates date/time of logical deletion/expiration. Cart is preserved for historic trace but not usable for active checkout.

commodities.description:
Array of commodities (cart items) placed in this cart instance. Each item corresponds to a composition of sale snapshot+options for checkout, following the IShoppingCartCommodity type.

Reference: `shopping_cart_commodities`.

IShoppingCart.ICreate.description:
Input/DTO for creating a new shopping cart in the shopping mall system.

Used by customer/seller/admin to initialize a new cart session per the shopping_carts business rules. Upon creation, cart is linked to the initiating actor as a new, empty, or optionally pre-filled structure.

Fields must conform to Prisma model for insertable properties.

Security: Only authorized actors may create valid carts—and only one active cart per context is typically allowed policy.

References: Prisma table shopping_carts.

shopping_customer_id.description: FK to the customer/connection requesting shopping cart creation. Must reference valid shopping_customers row in DB.

oneOf.description: Type of actor initializing the cart. Determines cart workspace and privilege context.

IShoppingCart.IUpdate.description:
Input/DTO for updating an existing shopping cart in the shopping_carts table.

Only permitted mutable fields are included (as per business requirements and evidence policy). Security validation restricts to genuine owner or privileged actor. Cannot update fields critical to relational or audit-trace context.

References: shopping_carts Prisma table.
Possible fields: logical deletion, actor type (if business allows), session-related meta.

Update scenarios may include marking deleted (soft delete), changing actor role (if admin-permitted), or restoring expired carts for analysis or testing.

deleted_at.description:
Timestamp to perform soft deletion of the cart, in line with evidence preservation and compliance audit rules.

Prisma: shopping_carts.deleted_at.

id.description:
장바구니 커머디티의 기본 키(UUID).

Prisma의 shopping_cart_commodities.id 컬럼 대응. 각 장바구니 아이템의 고유 식별자로 사용됩니다.

shopping_cart_id.description:
소속 장바구니의 ID.

shopping_carts.id를 FK로 참조합니다.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description:
대상 상품 스냅샷의 ID.

shopping_sale_snapshots.id를 FK로 참조합니다.

volume.description:
장바구니 커머디티에 담긴 수량.

단위: 세트(구성상품 기준), 1 이상의 자연수입니다.

장바구니 커머디티 상품 생성 시각.

Prisma의 created_at 컬럼에 해당합니다.

oneOf.description: 소프트 삭제 시점. 실제 삭제 대신 논리삭제로 관리합니다.

deleted_at.description: 소프트 삭제 시점. 실제 삭제 대신 논리삭제로 관리합니다.

IShoppingCartCommodity.description:
쇼핑몰 장바구니 내 개별 상품(커머디티) 정보의 전체 레코드를 표현하는 타입입니다.

Prisma shopping_cart_commodities 테이블의 실제 DB 컬럼과 1:1로 매칭되며, 기본 키(id), 장바구니 참조, 판매스냅샷 참조, 수량(volume), 생성일시, 삭제일시, 주문변환여부(published) 등이 존재합니다. 또한 관련 엔티티인 stock, order_goods 배열 등도 구조에 포함합니다. 본 타입은 주문 전 상품구성, 장바구니 내 다양한 아이템, 옵션, 스냅샷 기반 증거 데이터 관리 등 e커머스 업무 도메인의 핵심을 나타냅니다.

IShoppingCartCommodity.IRequest.description:
검색 및 필터 그리고 페이징을 위한 장바구니 상품 요청 데이터 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodities의 레코드를 대량으로 조회할 때 사용되는 필터링 및 옵션 정보를 담고 있으며, 각 필드는 실제 Prisma DB의 shopping_cart_commodities 테이블의 컬럼 또는 그와 연결된 엔티티 특성과 1:1로 매칭되어 상세히 설계되어 있습니다. 이 타입은 프론트엔드와 관리자, 관리자 API 모두에서 고도의 검색 기능 및 대용량 데이터 처리를 위해 사용됩니다.

IPageIShoppingCartCommodity.description:
shopping_cart_commodities 장바구니 상품 페이징 결과 컨테이너 타입입니다.

pagination 필드로 페이지 정보를, data 배열로 실제 장바구니 상품 엔티티 레코드들을 담고 있어, RESTful 검색 결과 및 페이징 처리에서 표준 결과 객체로 사용됩니다. pagination과 data의 내부 타입은 IPage 정책에 따라 설계되어 있습니다.

shopping_cart_id.description: 대상 장바구니의 ID. 반드시 존재하는 shopping_carts.id를 참조해야 합니다.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description: 담을 상품(판매스냅샷)의 ID.

volume.description: 장바구니에 추가할 상품의 수량(1 이상 자연수).

IShoppingCartCommodity.ICreate.description:
새로운 장바구니 상품(커머디티) 추가 시 요청에 사용되는 데이터 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodities에 신규 아이템을 추가할 때 요구되는 필수/선택 필드(장바구니ID, 스냅샷ID, 수량)를 담으며, 실제 엔티티의 컬럼 및 업무 정책을 충실히 반영하였습니다. 입력 검증, 참조 무결성 확인 등 백엔드 비즈니스 로직에 연계됩니다.

shopping_sale_snapshot_id.description: 변경할 경우 새로운 상품 스냅샷 ID.

volume.description: 수량 변경 시 새 값(1 이상 자연수).

IShoppingCartCommodity.IUpdate.description:
장바구니 상품(커머디티) 정보 변경 시 사용되는 요청 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodities 엔티티의 수량, 스냅샷 참조, 상태 변경 등 수정 가능한 컬럼들의 변경을 이 타입을 통해 전달합니다. 변경 가능한 필드만 선택적으로 전달되며, 미전달 시 기존값 유지 정책입니다. 프론트엔드, 앱, 관리자 모두에서 공통 활용합니다.

IShoppingCartCommodityStock.IRequest.description:
장바구니 커머디티-개별 유닛 스톡 정보 조회 및 검색을 위한 요청 데이터 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodity_stocks 테이블의 개별 상품유닛-재고 정보 목록을 검색할 때, 장바구니 커머디티 ID, 유닛ID, 스톡ID, 수량, 시퀀스 등 상세 필터조건을 포함하며, 대량 검색, 관리자 진단, 분석, 통계 처리에 폭넓게 쓰입니다.

IPageIShoppingCartCommodityStock.description:
장바구니 커머디티-개별유닛재고 리스트 페이징 컨테이너 타입입니다.

IPage 정책에 따라 페이지네이션(pagination) 정보와 배열(data)을 포함하여, 장바구니 내 옵션/유닛별 재고 정보 다건 검색 및 페이징 구현에서 표준적으로 사용됩니다.

id.description:
장바구니 커머디티-유닛재고 기본키(UUID).

shopping_cart_commodity_stocks.id 컬럼 1:1 대응.

quantity.description: 구매(주문/커머디티) 시 속한 유닛-스톡의 개수(재고, 1 이상).

sequence.description: 장바구니 커머디티 내 옵션, 유닛, 스톡 순번.

IShoppingCartCommodityStock.description:
장바구니 내 개별 상품유닛/재고 단위 정보를 담는 대표 엔티티 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodity_stocks 테이블 컬럼(커머디티 참조, 유닛 참조, 스톡 참조, 수량, 시퀀스 등)과 직접 매핑되며, 실제 장바구니 옵션선택, 수량관리, 유닛단위 연산 및 추적에 사용됩니다. 장바구니-주문, 옵션변경, 마이그레이션 등 광범위한 업무에서 중요한 역할을 합니다.

sequence.description: 해당 커머디티 내부 위치를 위한 순서값.

IShoppingCartCommodityStock.ICreate.description:
장바구니 커머디티 내 개별 유닛/재고 신규 추가 요청 데이터 타입입니다.

커머디티-개별유닛 스톡 신규 레코드 생성(상품유닛 및 스톡참조, 수량 등) 시 활용되며, 입력 검증, 중복체크, 수량정책 등 백엔드 비즈니스 로직과 연동됩니다.

sequence.description: 커머디티 내부 순서값 조정.

IShoppingCartCommodityStock.IUpdate.description:
장바구니 커머디티-유닛 스톡 정보 수정 요청 타입입니다.

커머디티 내 특정 옵션, 유닛-스톡 단위 수량/시퀀스 등의 변경작업을 위한 데이터 구조로, 선택적 필드 업데이트 방식을 따릅니다. 미전달값은 기존 데이터 유지 정책이며, 관리자/사용자/앱 공용으로 활용합니다.

IShoppingCartCommodityStockChoice.IReque.description:
장바구니 커머디티 스톡 옵션 선택 정보 목록 조회 및 검색 요청 타입입니다.

shopping_cart_commodity_stock_choices 엔티티의 대량 옵션선택 이력 및 설정 정보를 페이징, 필터링, 옵션ID, 후보ID 등으로 유연하게 검색할 수 있도록 설계되었습니다.

IPageIShoppingCartCommodityStockChoice.description:
장바구니 커머디티 옵션선택정보(choices) 페이징 결과 컨테이너입니다.

pagination 필드로 페이징 정보를, data 배열로 실제 옵션선택 엔티티 목록을 담아 API, 관리자, 통계 등 다양한 검색 UX에서 표준처럼 쓰입니다.

id.description: 장바구니 커머디티-스톡-옵션선택ID. 기본키 UUID.

oneOf.description: 옵션이 'select' 타입일 때 선택된 후보ID. 아닐 경우 null.

shopping_sale_snapshot_unit_option_candi.description: 옵션이 'select' 타입일 때 선택된 후보ID. 아닐 경우 null.
